We introduce HarnessMM (Harness Minus Minus), a method for improving harness token efficiency through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement (RSI). RSI iteratively refines companion harness configurations from training feedback, with validation selecting the configuration for deployment. A controller at the model-tool boundary reuses resolved decisions to replace later reasoning callbacks while actor weights remain fixed. Executable Decision Graphs store exact actions, literal arguments, causal dependencies, and public guards. Guarded Decision Reuse activates these persistent decisions from observed receipts; Certified Callback Substitution executes them through the native interface and records removal of the registered slow callback. New semantic decisions, unsupported evidence, and selector abstention invoke the original actor again. The representation restricts what feedback may change, while complete-task measurements establish quality and cost. On HumanEval, HarnessMM preserves Codex success at 90.82\% while reducing Tokens/task (k) from 66.72 to 47.02 (29.54\% saving). For DeepSeek Harness, success rises from 71.43\% to 85.71\% while Tokens/task (k) fall from 96.28 to 11.62 (87.93\% saving). A separate MBPP ablation measures 26.91\% lower cost than single-use graphs and 19.52\% lower cost than retained callbacks. These results establish guarded decision reuse as a practical way to reduce repeated reasoning in existing harnesses.

authors.name: Feifei Gao
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Knowledge Distillation across Item and Code Spaces for Parallel Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation with semantic IDs represents each item as a sequence of discrete codes derived from its semantic representation and predicts these codes to generate recommendations. Existing semantic-ID recommenders are typically trained with hard labels for the observed next item. Although such supervision identifies the target, it provides no explicit distributional information about alternative items conditioned on the same user history. Sequential recommenders can supply this item-level predictive knowledge, but transferring it to semantic-ID generation is challenging because the teacher and student operate in item and code spaces, respectively. We propose two complementary knowledge-distillation objectives for parallel semantic-ID recommenders, which predict all code positions simultaneously without autoregressive prefix conditioning. Item Distribution Matching (IDM) reconstructs a catalogue-level item distribution from the student's parallel code predictions and aligns it with the teacher's item distribution. Code Marginal Matching (CMM) projects the teacher's item probabilities onto each code position using fixed item-to-code assignments, then matches the resulting code marginals to the corresponding student heads. Both objectives transfer the teacher's soft distributional knowledge while preserving the student's parallel prediction structure. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that both methods consistently outperform existing state-of-the-art approaches. On average, IDM improves Recall@10 by 15.39%, while CMM improves NDCG@10 by 8.28%. These results demonstrate that distillation in either reconstructed item space or code-marginal space can substantially strengthen hard-label supervision for parallel generative recommendation.

authors.name: Linxiang Peng
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Formal Grammars and Generating Functions: From Algebraic Structure to Non-Algebraic and Non-Derivable Series
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how the algebraic and analytic properties of ordinary length generating functions constrain the grammatical and computational complexity of formal languages. We review the Chomsky-Schutzenberger representation, DSV translations for unambiguous context-free grammars, and their stack-indexed extensions, distinguishing finite algebraic systems from more general constructions. Examples and a diagonal argument demonstrate that even a rational generating function need not determine a language's grammatical class. Our central computability result establishes that, for a recursively enumerable language, computability of its length-counting sequence is equivalent to decidability of membership. Consequently, if a recursively enumerable language has a D-finite length generating function over Q(z), it is decidable; equivalently, undecidable recursively enumerable languages cannot have D-finite length generating functions. We then examine coefficient growth and singularities through Pringsheim's theorem, the Polya-Carlson dichotomy, Hadamard gaps, and Siegel G-functions. The resulting picture is asymmetric: analytic properties provide useful one-way constraints on language computability, but length enumeration loses too much information to determine grammatical or computational complexity without additional assumptions.

papers.title: Matching Particle-Arrival Rates for Low-Count Image Denoising
papers.abstract: Low-count imaging arises when limited illumination or dose yields only a few detected particles in microscopy, such as photons or electrons, causing measurements to be dominated by signal-dependent Poisson shot noise. Supervised denoisers typically require paired clean and noisy observations, whereas many self-supervised approaches exploit spatial or temporal redundancy without directly estimating the underlying particle-arrival process. We introduce PARM, a self-supervised denoising framework based on particle-arrival-rate matching. By modeling particle accumulation over exposure as a Poisson counting process, PARM identifies the conditional particle-arrival-rate field with the posterior mean of the latent clean rate. Poisson thinning then splits each observation into complementary lower-exposure views that provide self-supervised rate targets for one another. In implementation, the network estimates the normalized spatial allocation of the conditional rate, while the observed total count determines its global particle mass. Experiments on synthetic data, natural-video sequences corrupted with Poisson noise, and real low-dose electron microscopy demonstrate leading or competitive performance while effectively preserving fine structures. PARM therefore provides a statistically grounded approach to low-count image denoising when clean references are unavailable.

authors.name: Huazhen Liu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Jizhou Li
authors.institution: City University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen Research Institute

papers.title: Neural-DISCO: Source-Conditioned Counterfactual Editing of Neural Population Activity
papers.abstract: Understanding how neural activity encodes behavioral and sensory variables is a key challenge in systems neuroscience. This requires models that go beyond predicting activity from labels and instead support source-conditioned counterfactual editing: given a recorded source response, we should be able to edit one measured behavioral or stimulus label and predict how neural activity would change while preserving other observed labels and source-specific variability not explained by the labels. Here, we introduce \textbf{Neural-DISCO}, a disentangled representation learning framework for counterfactual modeling of neural activity. Neural-DISCO partitions the latent space into label-specific components, each associated with an observed behavioral or stimulus label, together with a residual latent that captures variability not supplied through observed labels. Across simulated and real neural recording datasets, we show that this structure enables selective editing of measured labels to generate counterfactual neural responses while preserving the remaining content of the original activity. Further, to gain insight into how behavioral and stimulus labels are encoded at single-neuron resolution, we pair this disentangled framework with feature attribution methods that identify which neurons are most important for each label. We find that disentanglement enhances the recovery of known functional cell roles in both synthetic and real data. Together, these results support Neural-DISCO as a framework for counterfactual modeling of neural activity and provide a practical interface for probing how neural populations encode behavior and sensory information. Code is available at https://github.com/TangLab-UBC/Neural-DISCO-neurips.

authors.name: Xin Tang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: DotSpace: A New Kind of Network for People and Their Agents
papers.abstract: We introduce DotSpace, a network paradigm in which people and their agents participate as first-class members. Participants interact in persistent shared spaces, forming relationships, exchanging knowledge and taking action across ownership boundaries, while each owner retains authority over their own agents. In such a network, relationships can become channels for coordinated action: people and their agents share context, make decisions, create things and maintain ongoing commitments together, while their agents carry the work forward between people's visits. Our central proposition is that persistent networks of people and their agents can widen access to distributed capabilities and support increasingly complex collective activity. Over time, such networks may become environments in which knowledge, practices and capabilities develop, shaping both what participants can accomplish and how they organize their activity together.

authors.name: Qingyun Wu
authors.institution: Singapore University of Technology and Design

papers.title: Linear Stability and a Turning Point Principle for Barotropic Liquid Stars with a Free Boundary in General Relativity
papers.abstract: We study the linear stability of spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat steady states of the Einstein-Euler system describing a liquid star surrounded by vacuum. The equation of state has positive surface density, positive causal sound speed, and an asymptotically linear high-density limit. We construct the equilibrium family and derive the linearized equation with a Robin boundary condition. The linearized operator has discrete real spectrum, and its negative Morse index equals the number of growing modes. We prove that the linearized operator around steady states with large central redshift admits a growing mode, while such growing modes do not exist for steady states with small central redshift. A parameter derivative of the equilibrium family provides a regular interior zero solution of the linearized equation, whose boundary defect is a nonzero multiple of the parameter derivative of the total mass. This gives a turning point principle: the kernel is one-dimensional precisely at mass critical points, and the sign of the crossing eigenvalue is determined by the bending of the mass-radius curve.

papers.title: A Proximal Gradient Method for Nonconvex Nonsmooth Optimization with Applications
papers.abstract: We study a proximal-gradient method for the sum of a convex smooth function $g$ and a possibly nonconvex, nonsmooth, strongly quasar-convex regularizer. The gradient step is weighted by the quasar-convexity parameter, so, for step sizes in the descent range, the iteration decreases a weighted objective, while the unweighted sum serves for comparison. We establish a geometric envelope around every global minimizer of the unweighted objective, with an explicit radius independent of the step size; a common minimizer yields global linear convergence. We also prove that every critical point $u$ of the weighted objective lies within an explicit multiple of $\|\nabla g(u)\|$ from every global minimizer of the unweighted objective. Together with an optimized composite comparison, this yields asymptotic distance bounds. An example shows that the two objectives can have different critical points. For power-regularized least squares with powers between zero and one, descent provides a confinement ball for the sharp local modulus, and support identification combined with a KL argument yields whole-sequence convergence.

authors.name: Jose M. M. Brito
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

papers.title: Input Bias Correction in Gaussian Process Regression
papers.abstract: In traditional Gaussian process (GP) regression, the inputs are typically assumed to be known, and uncertainty enters only through the measurements. When scalar fields are mapped using GP regression with measurements obtained from a mobile sensor, the inputs correspond to the estimated pose of the mobile sensor. The goal in this letter is to understand how a recorded GP, trained on erroneous inputs (e.g., pose estimates from dead-reckoning), can be corrected in a numerically efficient way when better estimates of the inputs become available. In the developed bias-aware GP (Ba-GP) framework, the recorded GP posterior-mean gradient is used to propagate estimated input bias and noise into mean and covariance corrections. The resulting additive covariance structure is then exploited to develop numerically efficient first-order correction algorithms. A simulation study and an indoor light-intensity mapping experiment show that Ba-GP improves predictive accuracy and uncertainty calibration relative to noisy-input GP baselines, with an order-of-magnitude reduction in computational cost relative to full GP retraining.

papers.title: Galaxy Luminosity Functions at z~7-10 from Four Years of JWST Observations
papers.abstract: We present galaxy luminosity functions at $z\approx 7.4$ and 10 based on a comprehensive search for candidate galaxies at $6.4\lesssim z\lesssim11.3$ in JWST's public NIRCam data four years after its operation. Our work utilises nine fields covering $\sim$1,045~arcmin$^2$ in total, including seven blank fields and two galaxy cluster fields. Using the dropout technique, we selected 3,733 dropouts from the F090W passband and 2,396 dropouts from the F115W passband, which constitute the largest samples of candidate galaxies at $z\approx 7.4$ and $z\approx 10$ to date. Among these objects, 338 F090W-dropouts and 99 F115W-dropouts already have secure redshifts from JWST NIRSpec spectroscopy over four years, which we use to form two large spectroscopic subsamples to assess the magnitude-dependent contamination rates of their parent dropout samples. Our luminosity functions are based on the results after statistically correcting for both incompleteness and contamination. We find that the luminosity function at $z\approx 7.4$ can be well described by a conventional Schechter function but with a faint-end slope of $α=-1.70\pm0.16$ that is significantly shallower than most of the previous studies at $z\approx 7$--8. To verify this result, more imaging and spectroscopy at $\sim$30~mag will be needed. The luminosity function at $z\approx 10$, on the other hand, can hardly be fitted by a Schechter function but is more consistent with a power law in the form of $Φ(M)\propto 10^{-0.4(β+1)M}$, with the best-fit slope of $β=-2.36\pm0.16$. While such a behavior is largely driven by the high number densities at $M_{\rm UV}\lesssim -21.8$~mag, it is supported by the currently existing spectroscopic confirmations. Further spectroscopy at the bright end($\lesssim 26$~mag) will be needed to strengthen this result.

papers.title: Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens
papers.abstract: Single-cell perturbation screens are used to train and evaluate models of perturbation effects, and model scores are judged against the reproducibility of the measured effects. Reproducibility is usually judged by splitting each perturbation's cells into two random halves, assumed to be independent replicates. In pooled screens such as Perturb-seq, the cells carrying a guide RNA descend from a limited number of transduced cells, so two random halves contain the same clones: pseudoreplication whose unit is not marked in the data. Using null perturbations (no expected effect) as controls, we compared random halves with independent replicates from separate transductions, and tested directly with halves that differ only in their clones. In a genome-scale screen of primary T cells, null perturbations agreed between random halves almost always and between independent replicates only half the time, the rate expected from noise alone; more cells did not remove it. With halves that share no clone, split by the T-cell receptor constant region or by a clone barcode, the excess agreement largely disappeared. Under a simple model, consistent with a screen that recorded clones, its size equals the share of expression differences set by clones divided by the effective number of clones per perturbation; in cell lines an upper bound on it was small. In the T-cell screen, shared clones inflated benchmark ceilings and reliability labels, the more so in donors with fewer effective clones, and when a model's input and scoring answer come from one transduction, published models that predict effects in a new cell state scored well even on perturbations with no expected effect; for the model tested (STATE), the gain vanished with the same guide from another transduction as answer. Reproducibility is better judged across separate transductions than between random halves.

papers.title: Multi-Material Topology Optimization of Phononic Crystals for Targeted Elastic Wave Bandgap
papers.abstract: Phononic crystals are periodic elastic structures that exhibit frequency bandgaps within which elastic waves cannot propagate. The formation and width of these bandgaps depend on the spatial distribution of material properties within periodic phononic unit cells. In this work, we propose novel topology optimization formulations to achieve multi-material design of phononic crystals for bandgap optimization at targeted frequencies, where we discover the influence of spatially varying properties of base materials on the band structures that block and permit elastic wave propagation. Specifically, we model wave propagation by Floquet-Bloch theory and solve the resulting eigenvalue problem by the finite element method along the boundary of the irreducible Brillouin zone. We first propose a multivariate weight-based method via a novel interpolation scheme that maps the design variables of an arbitrary number of candidate materials into effective density and stiffness for elastic wave-propagation calculations, where bandgaps arise from the contrast in the stiffness and inertia among material constituents. We then develop two formulations for bandgap optimization. The first formulation maximizes the gap between two adjacent frequency bands using a bound-based approach, where we introduce two auxiliary scalar variables as additional design variables and incorporate them directly into the design objective, yielding a linear, differentiable design objective, with the eigenfrequencies entering the formulation through associated constraints. The second formulation places a bandgap over a user-defined target frequency range through a dynamic band-pairing strategy, where we adaptively identify the relevant pair of adjacent bands amid optimization iterations. Towards the end, we validate the bandgap performance of our designs against the transmission loss spectra computed from COMSOL Multiphysics.

authors.name: Ting Chen
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Candan Tamerler
authors.institution: The University of Kansas Cancer Center

papers.title: WiMoT: Replay-Free Continual Wi-Fi Sensing via Moment Transport
papers.abstract: Continual Wi-Fi sensing must learn new rooms or users (plasticity) while keeping earlier ones (stability), yet sensing nodes often cannot retain channel state information (CSI) for privacy and storage reasons. We propose WiMoT (Wi-Fi Moment Transport), which stores the per-class feature mean and covariance of every earlier domain instead of samples. Stored statistics become stale when the representation changes, so WiMoT restricts the change to an affine map on a frozen feature basis and applies the same map to the statistics, which then stay valid without old samples. Supervised contrastive learning learns the new domain, a closed-form loss on the stored statistics keeps earlier classes separable, and a Gaussian discriminant classifier refitted from the transported statistics predicts without domain identity. On 3DO, WiMANS, and Widar3.0, WiMoT reaches average final accuracies of 94.02%, 89.61%, and 95.16% with at most 0.58 percentage points (pp) of forgetting. On 3DO and Widar3.0 it is 3.77 and 13.11 pp ahead of the strongest of 21 baselines, which uses replay; on WiMANS it matches the strongest replay baseline in accuracy while reducing forgetting from 2.78 to 0.00 pp. Rank-32 covariance factors shrink the moment memory to 6.4% at a cost of at most 0.49 pp.

authors.name: Yang Cao
authors.institution: Hunan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: The upper bounds on occupancy fraction and variance fraction for linear regular uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: The hard-core model can be used to understand the number of independent sets in graphs in extremal graph theory. The occupancy and variance fractions are the expectation and variance, respectively, of the independent-set size, normalized by the number of vertices. We provide upper bounds on the occupancy and variance fractions of linear $d$-regular $r$-uniform hypergraphs for small positive fugacities. In proving these results, we use the cluster expansion and the abstract polymer models, two tools from statistical physics, to analyse auxiliary functions associated with independence polynomials, comparing their low-order coefficients and controlling the remainders uniformly in the number of vertices.

papers.title: Reconstructing the Jordan structure of $C^*$-algebras from the metric on positive unit spheres
papers.abstract: Let $A$ and $B$ be unital $C^*$-algebras, and let $\mathrm{S}_{A^+}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{B^+}$ denote their positive unit spheres. We first show that the diametral relation on the positive unit sphere already determines Jordan structure. More precisely, suppose that $Λ:\mathrm{S}_{A^+}\to\mathrm{S}_{B^+}$ is a bijection satisfying \[ \|Λ(u)-Λ(v)\|=1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \|u-v\|=1 \qquad (u,v\in\mathrm{S}_{A^+}). \] If $A$ has no two-dimensional irreducible $^*$-representation, then $A$ and $B$ are Jordan $^*$-isomorphic. Moreover, the Jordan $^*$-isomorphism can be chosen to be compatible with $Λ$ on the peak and zero projections of positive norm-one elements. The proof is based on recovering the order and orthogonality structure of Akemann closed projections in the bidual. As a main application, we give an affirmative answer to the positive-sphere extension problem for unital $C^*$-algebras of real rank zero. Namely, if $A$ has real rank zero (but could has two-dimensional irreducible $^*$-representations) and $Λ:\mathrm{S}_{A^+}\to\mathrm{S}_{B^+}$ is a surjective isometry, then $Λ$ extends to a Jordan $^*$-isomorphism from $A$ onto $B$.

papers.title: SKG in Practice: OOD Generalization Cases Across FourDomains
papers.abstract: This paper presents the engineering implementation methods of the SKG inference framework and provides complete case studies across four domains. Case 1, 2D Dissipative Mechanical System: OOD MSE is 1.69 to 4.12 times lower than the best neural baseline; the state-dependent metric yields a 10^8-order improvement under controlled conditions. Case 2, Target Detection Sim-to-Real: Real-machine mAP increases from 0.2564 to 0.4964 (+24.00 points, single-run experiment, 32 images, point estimate), and AP75 increases from 0.1736 to 0.5765 (+40.29 points), with no real-machine retraining required. Case 3, Sequence Modeling sine to square: OOD MSE is 0.0296 versus Transformer 0.0641 (mean of 5 seeds, p=0.024). Case 4, Molecular Dynamics MD17: ID@100 ADE is 0.0285 versus ESTAG 0.1467; OOD@100 is 0.0316 versus 0.1411 (single seed). For each case, we present the objective, applied SKG theory, parameter settings, baseline comparison protocol, data results, and sources of advantage. Following the cases, we provide the complete methodology: pre-validation, task invariant construction, three-stage training, residual training, and the four theorems and one proposition supporting these methods. This paper not only demonstrates effective configurations of SKG across four domains but also honestly reports the variance of single-run experiments, limitations of single-seed results, negative updates caused by parameterization mismatch, and practical experience of using engineering thresholds as diagnostic signals rather than hard constraints.

papers.title: Finiteness of Dziobek central configurations in the Newtonian five-body problem
papers.abstract: We prove that, for any five fixed strictly positive masses, the Newtonian central configurations of exact affine dimension three form finitely many similarity classes. The proof uses the Dziobek equations, two constant identities, and local analysis of zeros and poles on a compact complex curve.

papers.title: Real-Time Localisation of Dorsal Anatomical Regions on Dairy Cows in Commercial Rotary Parlours from RGB-D
papers.abstract: Automated monitoring of dairy cows increasingly measures one part of the body, such as the rump for temperature or the back for posture, yet the region itself is usually placed by hand. Existing systems either score the cow as a whole or detect sparse keypoints, often in controlled walkways, and neither yields the named region masks that such measurements need on a crowded commercial rotary platform. We present a perception front end that finds the target cow, ten bony landmarks and four named dorsal regions (withers, back, rump and tail-head) in one forward pass over a whole RGB-D frame. Colour and depth encoders are fused late and share one decoder with three heads. On an anatomical region dataset built on public rotary-parlour RGB-D images (538 annotated frames, cow-disjoint test set), the network (ConvNeXt-T backbone) reaches PCK@10 0.905 for landmarks and region IoU 0.70 to 0.91, and runs end to end in 26.4 ms per frame on a T4 GPU, against an 11 fps camera. Removing the region head costs 0.15 PCK@10 (ResNet-18), but a control shows that it mainly adds training signal: wider landmark heatmap targets recover the gain without it. Agreement between the two heads flags unreliable frames without labels. On our own rig at Western Australia's largest dairy farm, the ConvNeXt-T model transfers with ten labelled frames (PCK@10 0.85), and its regions are carried through depth into a radiometric thermal camera, giving one temperature per region and cow that is stable within a pass.

authors.name: Hai Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Weak-$L^\infty$ and BMO with Hausdorff Content
papers.abstract: The space of weak-$L^{\infty}$ on measure space was introduced by Bennett et al. (Ann. of Math., 113(1981), 601-611) and proved to contain the space of $L^\infty$ and possess the appropriate interpolation property. In this paper, we are aimed to continue this line of research on the Euclidean space $\mathbb R^n$ endowed with Hausdorff content, which is a low-dimensional outer measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and fails to be additive or absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measures. But low-dimensional subsets, such as fractals, of $\mathbb{R}^n$ are Hausdorff capacitable. Precisely, in the setting of Hausdorff content, an analogue of weak-$L^\infty$ is defined and proved to possess an improved Marcinkiewicz interpolation theorem. Moreover, we show that the space of functions with bounded mean oscillation associated to the Hausdorff content is embedded into this new weak-$L^\infty$ space by establishing a key estimate for the distribution via a packing condition. As a by-product, the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood operator on the space of weak-$L^{\infty}$ is established.

authors.name: Hao Guo
authors.institution: Hebei Normal University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yangzhi Zhang
authors.institution: Zhejiang DongFang Vocational and Technical College

authors.name: Ciqiang Zhuo
authors.institution: Key Laboratory of Computing and Stochastic Mathematics (Ministry of Education)

papers.title: Positive Planar Measures for Spectral Pinching and the Corrected BMV Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the corrected Bessis--Moussa--Villani pinching conjecture for all symmetrized word averages. For Hermitian matrices $A,B$ and $D=E_A(B)$, we construct a positive compactly supported measure $ζ_{A,B}$ on $\mathbb R^2$ such that \[ \Tr f(xA+yB)-\Tr f(xA+yD) =y^2\int_{\mathbb R^2}f''(xa+yb)\,dζ_{A,B}(a,b). \] Its total mass is $\frac12\|B-D\|_2^2$. This representation proves the corrected conjecture, including its equality cases, and gives a positive bivariate moment representation for the coefficient differences. We also derive complete monotonicity of normalized exponential pinching defects and a comparison with Lie--Trotter approximations. A one-dimensional second-order loss measure is obtained for trace-preserving conditional expectations on finite tracial von Neumann algebras. Finally, we relate $ζ_{A,B}$ to Heinävaara's tracial joint spectral measure by an explicit positive radial transform.

authors.name: Trung Dung Vuong
authors.institution: Le Hong Phong High School for the Gifted

papers.title: Exact Algorithms and Complexity of the Smallest Grammar Problem
papers.abstract: The Smallest Grammar Problem (SGP) asks for a smallest straight-line grammar generating a given string, with size measured by the total right-hand-side length. For an input of length $n\ge2$ over at most $σ$ symbols, where $2\leσ\le n$, let $R=\log_σn$. We give a deterministic exact algorithm running in $n^{O(1)}2^{O(n\log\log n/(R\sqrt{\log n}))}$ time and polynomial space, with constants independent of $σ$. This gives time $2^{O(n\log\log n/(\log n)^{3/2})}$ for fixed alphabets and $2^{O(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ for arbitrary alphabets, up to polynomial factors. The algorithm combines pairwise disjoint representative occurrences of dictionary strings, a sparse interval certificate, and the Boolean tensor contraction theorem of OpenAI. It explicitly enforces dictionary membership, rule boundaries, and the grammar-size budget. Independently of that contraction theorem, disjoint representatives yield exact algorithms in $O^*(1.872258^n)$ time and $2^{O((n/R)\log(R+1))}$ time using $O(n)$ words of space. Anchor-based grammar projections establish binary NP-completeness and reductions with tunable alphabet size. We state their consequences as unconditional quantitative transfers from SGP algorithms to sparse SAT algorithms, and quantify the additional loss from sparsifying general formulas.

papers.title: SREdit: Scene Response Guided Appearance Editing for Projection Mapping
papers.abstract: Projection-based appearance editing changes selected visual attributes of a physical object through projection mapping (PM). To display a desired appearance, PM typically uses projector compensation, which computes a projector input that counteracts the geometric and photometric distortions of the scene. Compensation can only approximate this appearance within the available projection range, and it cannot revise the appearance itself. Pretrained LLM-based image editors provide a direct way to produce the desired appearance from a text prompt or reference image; projector compensation can then attempt to reproduce the edited result through projection. However, these editors do not have an accurate measure of the scene geometry or scene response. Therefore, their outputs may contain geometric misalignment, inconsistent shading, or changes outside the available projection range, which downstream projector compensation cannot correct. To address this problem, we introduce SREdit, an efficient response-guided framework for projection-based appearance editing. SREdit estimates a scene response map from the reconstructed scene that reflects how strongly projected illumination can affect different surface regions. SREdit uses the source appearance to constrain the early sampling process and preserve registration with the fixed physical object, while the scene response map adapts the amount of editing across surface regions. Experiments across two pretrained image editors show that SREdit improves projected appearance quality and reproduction fidelity. It adds less than one second per image with negligible VRAM overhead. Participants also consistently preferred the results produced with SREdit in our user study.

authors.name: Yuchen Deng
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Asymptotic spectral properties and extreme eigenvalues of sample correlation matrices from nonstationary high-dimensional VAR processes
papers.abstract: We study the limiting spectral distribution and extreme eigenvalues of the sample correlation matrix $\hat{\boldsymbol{R}}$ from a high-dimensional vector autoregressive (VAR) processes. Depending on whether roots of the characteristic polynomial of given VAR lie on (nonstationary) or outside (super-nonstationary) the unit circle, $\hat{\boldsymbol{R}}$ presents different types of asymptotic spectral properties. Under both nonstationary and super-nonstationary regimes, the empirical spectral distribution of $\hat{\boldsymbol{R}}$ degenerates in probability to a point mass at zero. The rescaled extreme eigenvalues of $\hat{\boldsymbol{R}}$ are asymptotically equivalent to the eigenvalues of a finite-dimensional symmetric random matrix determined by the characteristic roots. Moreover, under super-nonstationarity, $\hat{\boldsymbol{R}}$ degenerates in probability to a matrix with finite rank.

authors.name: Ruihan Liu
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Chen Wang
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent - and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical
papers.abstract: AI systems that discover scientific relations now generate candidate "laws" at scale, but the bottleneck has shifted from generation to vetting: which candidates deserve belief? We show that a deployed self-improving science agent - one that has admitted 252 relations through held-out prediction courts - already computes the quantity that answers this question: the Minimum Description Length compression ratio used for model selection doubles, when read under discrete accounting, as an unsupervised epistemic grader. The compression-ranked top band of the agent's ledger recovers exactly the canonical laws among its discoveries (vis-viva across seven planets, Balmer/Rydberg) plus cross-measurement identities - enrichment $p=3.6\times10^{-12}$ under a hypergeometric test - with zero counterexamples and physically coherent band structure. The same lens retroactively reveals that 86% of the ledger compresses nothing ($\mathrm{cr}\approx 1$): the agent had been recording statistical regularities, including a learned predictor with held-out $R^2=0.541$ admitted through the prediction gate, under a narrative of compression as the unified value of knowledge - a narrative that was never true for them. We formalize the resulting dual-axis bookkeeping - prediction value ($R^2$) and compression value (cr) as nearly decoupled axes of knowledge - demonstrate its robustness to quantization, and register forward falsifiable predictions. The episode is, to our knowledge, the first measured instance of a discovery agent auditing its own knowledge ledger by an internal measure and finding itself over-claiming.

papers.title: Foundation Models Meet Power Grid Topology for Cascade Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate early-stage prediction of cascading failure severity is essential for assessing the vulnerability of power transmission networks. However, existing data-driven approaches often rely on network-specific representations, limiting their generalizability across power system topologies. This work investigates the complementary capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for cascading failure severity prediction. First, standalone LLM predictors are developed using a LoRA-fine-tuned LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct model with varying degrees of topological information. A hybrid Graph-LLM fusion framework is then proposed, integrating a Topology-Aware Graph Attention Transformer (TAGAT) with the LLM through confidence-gated fusion. TAGAT captures structural dependencies among transmission lines, while the LLM extracts representations from early-stage power-flow observations and aggregated cascade descriptors. The frameworks are evaluated on 30,000 simulated cascading failure scenarios for each of the IEEE 118-bus and IEEE 300-bus systems. Using only the first four cascade steps, the hybrid framework achieves weighted F1 scores of 0.94 and 0.92, respectively. In cross-system transfer from IEEE 118-bus to IEEE 300-bus, it achieves 0.72 zero-shot accuracy, improving to 0.83 with limited target-system calibration, outperforming standalone models and conventional baselines. These results show the potential of combining graph-based structural learning with foundation models to improve cascading failure severity prediction and cross-system transferability.

papers.title: A Compact Single-Beam Optically Pumped Magnetometer Based on Absorption Detection
papers.abstract: We demonstrate a compact single-beam optically pumped magnetometer (OPM) employing a pure 87Rb microfabricated vapor cell with 500 Torr buffer gas. The residual magnetic field is actively minimized to below 400 pT through a combination of mu-metal magnetic shielding and internal compensation coils. We systematically characterize the OPM response as a function of laser detuning and optical intensity, and derive the magnetic-field sensitivity from the signal slope and noise amplitude spectral density. A best sensitivity of 11 fT/Hz^1/2 is achieved near the resonance transition at an optimal optical intensity, using a small cell volume of only 0.027 cm^3. Furthermore, a miniaturized OPM prototype was developed using a folded flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) to integrate the vapor cell, a compact heater, and magnetic-field coils into a cubic sensing head. Two coil configurations patterned directly on the FPCB were investigated. Under optimized operating conditions, the OPM prototype achieved a sensitivity of 66 fT/Hz^1/2. These results demonstrate that high-buffer-pressure single-beam OPMs can achieve excellent sensitivity, establishing a pathway toward compact and scalable arrays.

authors.name: Yi-Hsuan Chen
authors.institution: Mackay Junior College of Medicine, Nursing and Management

papers.title: Long-time stability and convergence of a BDF3 method for a parabolic equation with fading memory
papers.abstract: We analyze the long-time stability and convergence of a third-order backward differentiation formula (BDF3) for parabolic equations with exponentially fading memory. The BDF3 scalar resolvent has oscillatory coefficients, so the monotonicity argument used for lower-order formulas in [Math. Comp. 62 (1994) 477-496] does not apply. We instead control memory feedback by the absolute mass of its discrete Green sequence and establish the rigorous stability-constant bounds $23/20<Λ_3<579/500$. A causal third-order memory quadrature with nonnegative assembled weights then yields exponentially weighted stability without a parabolic step-size restriction. With third-order starting values, we prove a uniform-in-time third-order temporal error estimate and extend it to conforming finite elements. Numerical tests confirm the predicted convergence orders and the long-time behavior.

papers.title: Schur--Weyl duality for coideal subalgebras of quantum affine superalgebras of type $A$
papers.abstract: We extend the results of \cite{FLLLWW20} to the super setting. More precisely, we define two families of coideal sub-superalgebras of quantum affine superalgebras of type $A$, called $\jmath$- and $\imath$-quantum affine superalgebras respectively, and establish Schur--Weyl duality between them and affine Hecke algebras of type $C$.

papers.title: CFBrainAug: Modularity-Induced Counterfactual Brain Network Augmentation for Interpretable fMRI-based Autism Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Machine learning on resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) brain networks is promising for diagnosing Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), but existing methods are prone to overfitting on limited training data, and their post-hoc statistical attribution offers limited clinical interpretability. We propose CFBrainAug, a counterfactual brain network learning framework that unifies data augmentation and counterfactual explanation by learning label-altered brain networks. Unlike conventional label-preserving augmentation, CFBrainAug first retrieves a label-opposite yet topologically similar candidate and then refines it under a module-number constraint. Jointly training on factual and counterfactual networks enriches the training distribution around the decision boundary, enabling a lightweight feature-selection-based SVM to perform competitively with recent graph deep learning methods. Meanwhile, the counterfactuals provide intrinsic explanations by identifying the connectivity differences between each subject and its counterfactual. Experiments on the ABIDE I dataset show that CFBrainAug reaches an accuracy of 74.1% on the NYU site, suggesting that counterfactual augmentation can complement more complex models in small-sample brain network analysis.

papers.title: Lacunary maximal operators on convex boundaries
papers.abstract: We disprove the cap-sufficiency proposal in Wright's Problem 16 for $1<p<(\sqrt{13}-1)/2$ and for $p>3$. For each fixed exponent in these ranges, one smooth strictly convex domain has finite original directional cap integral, while the lacunary maximal operator of complete arclength fails restricted weak type. We also give a geometric sufficient condition for strong $L^p$ boundedness, for every finite $1<p<\infty$, on an arbitrary given bounded convex domain. It requires one logarithmic integral of a curvature lower envelope, without a differentiability assumption on the boundary or a restriction on the number of curvature zeros. Both results concern unnormalised true arclength, one fixed interior origin and all integer dyadic dilations.

authors.name: Xi Cen
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology

papers.title: PoKER: A Probability of Kill Estimation Rate Model for Air-to-Air Missiles Using Machine Learning on Stochastic Targets
papers.abstract: This work introduces PoKER, a novel probabilistic model engineered to optimize missile launch effectiveness in air-to-air scenarios, specifically within Beyond Visual Range (BVR) air combat. Unlike conventional Weapon Engagement Zone (WEZ) models that delineate zones based on static distances such as maximum, minimum, and no-escape ranges, PoKER applies machine learning to predict kill probabilities more accurately by integrating the stochastic behaviors of targets and missile miss distances. This model dynamically evaluates target behavior, greatly expanding the predictive capabilities of engagement analysis. By factoring in elements such as warhead lethality, target and shooter orientations, and the specific conditions of engagement, PoKER provides important insights into engagement dynamics and quantifies success probabilities. Consequently, it can potentially be an important tool for BVR air combat pilots, improving operational decision-making within this specialized combat domain.

authors.name: Diego Geraldo
authors.institution: Instituto de Estudos Avançados da Universidade de São Paulo

papers.title: On polarizations of affine Calabi--Yau varieties
papers.abstract: Let $(X, Ω)$ be an affine Calabi--Yau variety, by which we mean a klt affine variety $X$ with a non-vanishing algebraic volume form $Ω$. In connection with complete Calabi--Yau metrics of Euclidean volume growth on $(X, Ω)$, we study algebraic aspects of polarizations of $X$ given by a negative valuation. We show that such a valuation is finitely generated with a klt degeneration if and only if $X$ admits a dlt log Fano type compactification, generalizing a compactification considered by Tian--Yau. We further give a valuative criterion detecting K-semistability of the degeneration by a negative valuation.

authors.name: Yueqiao Wu
authors.institution: Qingdao University of Science and Technology

papers.title: One-Million-Year-Old Nascent Eclipsing Binaries in the LMC
papers.abstract: The light curves of nascent eclipsing binaries (EBs) feature sinusoidal reflection effects as a hot B-type main-sequence (MS) primary irradiates the near side of a cool, low-mass, pre-MS companion. We obtained multi-epoch echelle spectra with the MIKE spectrograph on the 6.5m Magellan-Clay Telescope of three nascent EBs embedded in H II regions within the LMC. By fitting atmospheric models to the spectra, the primaries are found to be mid-B dwarfs (T_eff,1 = 18,600-22,800 K; M_1 = 6.8-8.5 Msun). The dynamical masses of the secondaries are only M_2 = 0.38-0.95 Msun, yielding extremely small mass ratios q = M_2/M_1 = 0.05-0.11. Unlike solar-type primaries, which exhibit a dearth of close companions with q < 0.1 known as the brown dwarf desert, massive stars can readily form with very close companions below q < 0.1. By fitting PHOEBE models to the OGLE-III light curves, we measure the secondary radii R_2 = 2.0-2.8 Rsun and temperatures T_eff,2 = 4,000 K. The pre-MS companions are located high on the Hayashi track where evolutionary models indicate ages of only 1 Myr. Their extreme youth suggests that nascent EBs formed via inward disk migration during the previous embedded protostellar phase.

papers.title: Global recovery of a scalar diffusivity from a single final state
papers.abstract: We prove global uniqueness and Lipschitz stability for a scalar diffusivity in the heat equation from a single final state at any prescribed positive time. On each prescribed uniformly elliptic $C^{1,α}$-bounded class with known coefficient boundary values, we choose a constant initial datum and a spatially constant exponential boundary input that work for the entire class. The result holds on smooth bounded connected domains in every dimension $n\ge2$ and gives an affirmative answer to \cite[Problem~8.2]{Alessandrini} within these classes. The stability estimate controls the $L^2$ diffusivity difference by the $H^2$ final-state difference, and this data norm is optimal within the Sobolev scale for the chosen experiment.

papers.title: PCFBench: How Far Can Large Vision-Language Models Go in Physics-aware Photonic Inverse Design?
papers.abstract: Photonic crystal fibers (PCFs) underpin critical applications in telecommunications, sensing, and high-power laser delivery, yet their design remains a manual, expert-intensive process that couples geometric intuition with deep waveguide physics. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer a promising path toward automating PCF design, but can they truly reason about photonic physics from microscopy images, or do they merely recognize visual patterns? We introduce PCFBench, the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating VLMs on the perception, reasoning, and decision steps of the photonic inverse-design loop. PCFBench spans 26 tasks organized into six categories of increasing cognitive demand (Geometry Perception, Physics Understanding, Text Generation, Multi-modal Reasoning, Inverse-Design Decision, and Code Generation), built from over 220K FDTD simulation samples across 18 structurally diverse fiber families. We evaluate both individual VLMs on isolated tasks and multi-agent systems (MAS) on the full sequential pipeline from perception to design. Our results reveal a striking perception-design gap: current models can identify fiber geometry with moderate success, yet consistently fail to translate that visual understanding into physics-aware design actions. Moreover, cascading agents through the pipeline exposes significant error propagation, where upstream perception mistakes compound into downstream design failures. These findings suggest that neither model scaling nor naive agent chaining suffices, and that closing the loop demands explicit physical grounding. PCFBench provides the community with a rigorous, multi-dimensional testbed to measure progress toward AI-assisted photonic engineering. The project is available at https://pcfbench.github.io/.

papers.title: DeepAVR: Deep Analysis via Multi-Agent Collaboration for Automated Vulnerability Repair
papers.abstract: Automated Vulnerability Repair (AVR) has emerged as a critical defense against software security flaws, aiming to triage and fix bugs autonomously. Early LLM-based approaches focused on patch generation under the assumption of perfect fault localization, while recent end-to-end methods attempt to repair vulnerabilities directly from sanitizer logs. However, these methods often fail when the root cause is deeply hidden--either physically distant from the crash site or logically masked by interdependent errors--making the initial report insufficient. We propose DeepAVR, a multi-agent framework for end-to-end AVR that performs deep analysis by transforming intermediate repair outcomes into structured diagnostic feedback. DeepAVR decomposes repair into specialized roles--Fault Localization, Patch Generation, Compile Validation, Security Validation, Functionality Validation, and Patch Review--and routes feedback across these roles to iteratively refine both localization and patch hypotheses. In particular, DeepAVR introduces patch-conditioned re-localization, which treats execution results from intermediate patches as diagnostic signals to uncover hidden root causes, and a root-cause-oriented patch review stage that detects symptom-level fixes and incomplete repairs beyond execution-based validation. Evaluation on the real-world C/C++ vulnerability repair dataset VulnLoc shows that DeepAVR significantly outperforms prior methods, generating correct patches for 92.3% of vulnerabilities. Furthermore, results on SAN2VULN demonstrate strong generalization, with DeepAVR effectively repairing vulnerabilities unseen during training.

papers.title: Patronizing and Condescending Language Detection in English and Mandarin
papers.abstract: Patronizing and condescending language (PCL) is a form of harmful language that belittles and assumes pity for vulnerable groups, reinforcing negative societal stereotypes. However, unlike overt hate speech, it is often difficult to detect, even for human judges. This paper proposes a system for the automated detection of PCL. Our first approach uses static word embeddings and a convolutional neural network for classification, while our second approach uses pre-trained BERT embeddings fine-tuned for the PCL task. Our second approach was considerably more successful, and achieved an F1 score of 0.528 over the development set.

papers.title: Superlinear Convergence of Cyclic Gradient Methods with Historical Ritz Step Sizes
papers.abstract: Simplified spectral models predict dimension-dependent superlinear convergence for gradient methods, but the corresponding behavior of actual iterations remains only partially understood. Historical methods introduce an additional difficulty: the gradients defining the step sizes differ from those receiving them. We study this offset for cyclic reuse of historical Ritz step sizes on strictly convex quadratics. Within the existing limited memory steepest descent with retards (LMSDR) family, a rolling cyclic Ritz (RCR) rule reuses $m$ historical Ritz values $\ell$ times per cycle, ending with a complete sweep. At $q=m+1$ active distinct eigenvalues, an exact delayed recurrence gives almost-everywhere doubly exponential convergence with an explicit rate and exceptional weights. Nonempty open basins also exist for $m+1<q\le2m$ and $\ell\ge4$. Rebuilding the history from each cycle-start gradient costs $m$ additional updates and gives sampled cyclic Ritz reuse (SCR) a cycle-end map determined by the current weights. Under uniform sampling bounds, SCR converges doubly exponentially almost everywhere when $(2\ell-1)^m>\binom{q-1}{m}$. Increasing $\ell$ admits larger $q$ for fixed $m$. The guarantee extends to history-dependent choices from finite sampling menus under a bound on the number of admissible sampling sequences. Geometrically spaced decisions retain the SCR condition and rate range. Every update is counted, including sampling; a numerical illustration compares finite-tolerance update counts.

papers.title: Geometry property of stochastic parabolic equations and Prékopa-Leindler inequality on bounded domains
papers.abstract: We study the preservation of spatial concavity and log-concavity for stochastic parabolic equations posed on bounded convex domains. For the linear noise, by using Minkowski convolutions, we establish the convexity preservation of solution almost surely. For the nonlinear noise, by using Itô formula, the impact of noise is given. Moreover, we establish the relationship between the weighted (stochastic) Prékopa-Leindler inequality and properties of (stochastic) parabolic equation on bounded domain, which is new even for deterministic case.

authors.name: Guangying Lv
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Trusting the Tool: Asymmetric Deference of LLM Vulnerability Auditors to Static-Analysis Evidence
papers.abstract: Pipelines that combine large language models (LLMs) with static analysis let the model consume the analyser's output as evidence, but whether the model distinguishes true from false evidence, and whether its scrutiny depends on what the evidence claims, has not been measured. We built an intraprocedural analyser for C/C++ that produces proof obligations and audited vulnerable and patched functions from PrimeVul under six evidence conditions that differ only in the notes, including fabricated assurances that a missing check exists and fabricated alarms that an added check is missing. The study covers 916 pairs in four disjoint sets, eleven model configurations from four vendors and 16,572 audits; no model is trained or fine-tuned. True evidence barely improved accuracy (+0.02). False evidence acted asymmetrically: relative to true notes about the same operations, false assurances lowered the detection of real vulnerabilities by up to 19 points, whereas false alarms never significantly lowered accuracy and were disputed far more often. An internally registered replication on seven new models confirmed that false assurances move verdicts towards their claim more than false alarms do (mean asymmetry +0.16, 95% CI +0.10 to +0.24). Instructions in the audit prompt did not reliably reduce deference; the best one failed to replicate. Verifying each claim in a separate call and showing the refuted claims raised accuracy under false assurances by 12 points in a pre-specified test (p=0.002) without loss under true evidence; for a second model the gain was smaller and not significant. Pipelines should therefore verify a tool's guarantees before the model relies on them, and studies should measure deference in a direction-aware way.

papers.title: The chromatic number of $\{\mathrm{ISK}_4, \textup{diamond}\}$-free graphs
papers.abstract: An $\mathrm{ISK}_4$ is a graph that is isomorphic to a subdivision of $K_4$; a \textit{diamond} is $K_4$ minus one edge; and a \textit{bowtie} consists of two triangles sharing exactly one vertex. Lévêque, Maffray, and Trotignon~(2012) conjectured that every $\mathrm{ISK}_4$-free graph is $4$-colorable. Chen, Chen, Cui, Feng, and Liu~(2021) proved this for $\{\textup{diamond},\textup{bowtie}\}$-free graphs. We prove this conjecture for diamond-free graphs. Moreover, the bound is optimal.

authors.name: Qing Cui
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

papers.title: Natural-Language to Nav2: Operational Policies for Costmap-Based Navigation
papers.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots support material transport in warehouses and industrial facilities, where navigation must adapt to changing operating conditions. Sensor observations reveal physical obstacles, but do not by themselves specify temporary access rules, route preferences, or exceptions known to operators. This paper presents a natural-language policy interface that brings this knowledge into ROS 2 Nav2. A local large language model converts instructions into JSON policies specifying destinations, spatial constraints, and temporal or event conditions. Deterministic checks govern mission acceptance, and three costmap adapters project accepted policies into the existing navigation stack without changing its planner or controller. On 150 researcher-authored English commands, four local models produce 107-142 correct accepted policies, compared with 44 for a rule-based parser, with 3-20 incorrect acceptances per model. Fault injection records rejection of eight endpoint/JSON faults and 29 validator-stage faults. Navigation experiments use correct task policies to evaluate keepouts, zone costs, person-dependent regions, and event-conditioned passage in simulation and on a TurtleBot3. For Tasks 1-3, mean travel times are 18.4-24.5% lower in simulation and 23.1-35.0% lower on the physical testbed than with the baseline lacking those policies. A native KeepoutFilter comparison and two-robot demonstrations examine basic keepout behavior and shared policy projection. The interface connects operator instructions to explicit navigation policies while retaining Nav2's planning and control components.

authors.institution: Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Kyung-Joon Park
authors.institution: Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Retiming Robot Demonstrations with a Learned Speed Prior
papers.abstract: The pace of a robot demonstration is often determined by the teleoperator rather than by the task itself. As a result, the same motion can appear at widely different speeds across demonstrations, and policies trained on such data may inherit operator-specific timing along with task behavior. We propose to learn a speed prior directly from large-scale demonstration data. Given a task instruction, a motion path and the images along it, it predicts a distribution over execution speed along the path, from which a chosen quantile defines a consistent clock for retiming each demonstration. Existing methods derive the acceleration signal from the very data they accelerate, so each new task costs another fit, annotation, or pair of predefined rates. A single trained speed prior instead covers every task in a corpus. We fit a speed prior on both robot teleoperation data and handheld demonstrations in which a human arm, rather than a robot arm, moves the gripper, and use it to retime robot demonstrations to the handheld pace before fine-tuning a vision-language-action policy. For execution, we pair the policy with a real-time optimal-control layer that tracks predicted action chunks under robot constraints using the predicted pace. On 120 RoboLab tasks, policies fine-tuned on our learned clocks succeed more often and move with up to half the jerk compared with policies fine-tuned on the original demonstration timing and uniformly accelerated to the same speed. On a real robot, our policy stacks cups in 3.50s, 1.72$\times$ faster than the default policy's 6.02s while succeeding as often, in 29 of 30 trials. Videos and further material are available at https://mllab.snu.ac.kr/projects/learned_speed_prior.

papers.title: Interpreting Physics in Video Encoders using Multi-Object Interaction Videos
papers.abstract: Video encoder models are increasingly used as world models for physical AI, where a policy plans by rolling out the latent, so what physics the latent holds bounds what the agent can plan over. Moreover, existing interpretability work probes quantities belonging to a single object; the quantities that make physics relational, such as momentum transfer, restitution, and friction, are defined between bodies and have not been examined. We probe relational physics attributes in two frozen self-supervised video encoders (V-JEPA2 and VideoMAE) under two-body settings and test if they transfer across environments. Our early findings are mixed. Both encoders separate elastic from inelastic collisions reliably. V-JEPA2's own predictor is less likely to predict a collision that creates kinetic energy compared to one that loses it. Momentum-violation detection appears in only one of the two encoders, a kinetic-energy readout survives a change of environment for V-JEPA2 but not for VideoMAE, and neither model holds a friction coefficient that survives a change of geometry.

papers.title: Tilt, warp, and dissipation flare in hydrodynamic disks around kicked compact objects
papers.abstract: We study the dynamical response of a hydrodynamic disk to an impulsive kick imparted to a central massive object, focusing on the global properties of the material that remains gravitationally bound. We construct a simple analytic model and show that the bound material can acquire a significant tilt---or even a retrograde rotation---if the kick is directed close to the disk midplane. We perform 3D numerical simulations and show that (1) the bound material relaxes to a torus-like circularized flow of which total mass and angular momentum is in fair agreement with the analytic estimate, and (2) in spite of nonlinear hydrodynamic effects, a highly tilted or retrograde disk can be sufficiently formed. The simulations additionally reveal a transient warp in the kicked disk, suggesting a kick as a formation mechanism of tilted or warped disks around compact objects. About 10% of the kinetic energy the bound material acquired from the kick is converted to the internal energy, while the exact conversion efficiency depends on the kick angle and the initial surface mass density profile. The luminosity of this kick-driven dissipation flare can reach $\sim 10^{43}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ for strong kicks ($V_{\rm kick} \sim 1000$km/s). We discuss the implications of our results for recoiling supermassive black holes, recoiled stellar-mass black holes in the disks of active galactic nuclei, and natal kicks on compact objects.

papers.title: Polychromatic blocks and explicit lower bounds for multicolour van der Waerden numbers
papers.abstract: Let $W(r,k)$ be the least $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ contains a monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progression. Many of the best lower bounds for $W(r,k)$ with $r\ge3$ come from blow-up recurrences of Blankenship, Cummings and Taranchuk and of Xu, in which a known colouring is lengthened by a periodic block. Call an $h$-colouring of $Z_q$ $k$-polychromatic if every $k$-term progression with nonzero common difference meets each of the $h$ colours. The argument behind these recurrences shows that such a colouring gives $W(r,k)>q(W(r-\lceil r/h\rceil,k)-1)$ for all $r\ge h$. We show that cubic, quartic, quintic and sextic residue colourings give $k$-polychromatic blocks with $q$ much larger than $k$ (e.g. $q=1,376,317$ for $h=3$ and $k=28$), and use them to get explicit lower bounds. For three colours and $9\le k\le28$ we improve on every published bound we know of, among them $W(3,9)>4,002,705$ and $W(3,28)>159,594,201,561,100,726$. For $3\le r\le6$ and $9\le k\le28$, $77$ of the $80$ cases improve on what the published bounds give under these recurrences and the other three tie. For $r=5$ and $12\le k\le15$ the best values come from palettes that are cyclic intervals of colours indexed by quintic residues. We checked every block by exhaustive enumeration and every base colouring by computer. We also prove that the block modulus is at most $(W(2,k)-1)/(k-1)$, so the method does not improve the asymptotics. For large $k$ the largest cubic block modulus lies between $k^{4-\varepsilon}$ and $k^2 4^k$.

papers.title: Tropical cohomology for band schemes over the tropical hyperfield
papers.abstract: We define tropical band varieties as $\mathbf{T}$-reductions of separated finitely presented $\mathbf{T}$-band schemes. We construct a faithful functor from the category of tropical band varieties to the category of extended polyhedral spaces in the sense of Gross--Shokrieh. As a byproduct, we show that tropical cohomology can be defined functorially on tropical band varieties.

papers.title: Rethinking Representation Geometry in Supervised Contrastive Learning under Long-Tailed Data
papers.abstract: Supervised contrastive learning and its balanced variants have demonstrated their effectiveness for representation learning under long-tailed distributions. However, although prior analyses suggest that their optimal representations may exhibit a regular simplex geometry, whether such a geometry is indeed exhibited remains insufficiently understood. In this work, we present a theoretical framework for these objectives that characterizes whether a regular simplex is formed at the optimum. By applying this to representative objectives, we show that these objectives fail to form a regular simplex at the optimum because they remain dependent on the number of samples per class. Motivated by this analysis, we introduce structural balancing that can be applied to contrastive objectives, and propose a fully balanced contrastive objective that provably forms a regular simplex geometry at its optimum. Both theoretical and empirical results demonstrate that the proposed method yields a more balanced representation space and improves performance on long-tailed recognition and transfer learning tasks.

papers.title: Imaginary elements and crystals for quantum groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of stable imaginary elements in quantum groups and use crystal basis theory to construct explicit one-parameter families of such elements for all finite types. We show that all of Leclerc's examples of imaginary elements are stable imaginary. Using the generalized quantum Schur--Weyl duality, we also construct explicit examples of corresponding imaginary modules over quantum affine algebras of untwisted affine types.

authors.name: Kyu-Hwan Lee
authors.institution: Korea Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: X-Dubbing: Speech-to-Speech Translation under Temporal and Visual Constraints
papers.abstract: Cross-lingual dubbing aims to convert source speech into target-language speech that remains synchronized with the original video. The key to this task is to produce a faithful translation that is naturally speakable within the source timing, which is non-trivial because languages differ in duration, rhythm, and articulation. In this paper, we propose X-Dubbing, which formulates the task as a joint problem of time-aware speech-to-text translation and video-aware text-to-speech. Specifically, our method consists of a Dubbing Translator that generates temporally structured scripts and a Voice Actor that renders them in synchrony with the source video, both grounded in a language-agnostic timing budget. We further refine the translator with dubbing-aware feedback from the synthesized speech, encouraging scripts that yield well-synchronized dubbing. This design requires no paired dubbing data, as the two components are trained on speech-text and monolingual audio-visual data respectively. Extensive experiments show that X-Dubbing outperforms recent baselines across diverse metrics, including isochrony and audio-visual correspondence.

authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Continuous-Time Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Control: Limits, Duality, and Stability
papers.abstract: A sampled robust control problem averages future values over disturbance laws, while its continuous-time counterpart evolves with an averaged drift. We establish a fluid limit connecting these two models for Wasserstein ambiguity sets. Under a uniform disturbance moment bound and subcritical growth, sampled Bellman values converge locally uniformly to the upper and lower values of a discounted differential game. The argument accommodates unbounded disturbances without requiring square-integrable increments. We also derive an explicit bound on the change in either game value when both the radius and center of the ambiguity set vary. For Euclidean disturbance space, uniform Lipschitz continuity in the disturbance, common state and cost Lipschitz bounds, and a discount rate exceeding the drift's state Lipschitz constant, this estimate converts distributional confidence bounds into uniform value approximation bounds. Static Wasserstein duality reformulates pointwise distributional optimization; affine disturbance dependence permits an exact reduction to a ball of means. Experiments illustrate the common limit and decreasing value error with sample size. For a nonlinear disturbance model, uniform shifts overestimate worst-case recovery speed by about 36\%. In a two-product inventory model, increasing ambiguity raises production near balance while reducing the region of full production in deeper backlogs.
