papers.title: Minimal Surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with Three Planar Ends II: Symmetry and Nonexistence
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study complete minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with three embedded planar ends parallel to those of the union of the Lagrangian catenoid and the plane containing its waist circle. We prove that no such complete embedded minimal surface of genus $g\geq 2$ with finite total curvature admits at least $4(g+1)$ symmetries. This contrasts sharply with the genus-one case, where highly symmetric examples do exist and are uniquely determined up to scaling and rigid motion.

papers.title: NECTAR: Automatic Negative Clue Estimation via Centroid-Space Mapping for Target Speaker Extraction
papers.abstract: Target speaker extraction (TSE) aims to extract a desired speaker from a mixture using auxiliary clues such as enrollment speech. An interferer-related representation can provide a useful negative clue for TSE, but such information is not directly available from the target enrollment. To derive this representation from the observed mixture, we analyze the relationship between the speaker representations of a speech mixture and its constituent speakers. Our analysis shows that the mixture centroid lies near the midpoint of its constituent speaker centroids, whereas this relationship does not hold for single-utterance embeddings. Based on this observation, we propose NECTAR, NEgative Clue for TARget speaker extraction, which automatically derives an interferer-related negative clue from the mixture using the centroid-space relationship. We further introduce a Centroid-Space Mapper (CSM) to estimate the required centroid representations from a mixture and a target enrollment. NECTAR achieves the highest SI-SDRi on Libri2Mix among the compared systems trained on LibriSpeech train-clean-100, reaching 16.18 dB.

authors.name: Hyungjun Yoo
authors.institution: Korea Institute of Radiological and Medical Sciences

authors.name: Jung-Woo Choi
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Watermarking Diffusion Language Models with Learned Foresight and Balanced Bands
papers.abstract: Green-red watermarks favor tokens from a green list that a secret key derives from the preceding tokens. Diffusion language models, however, often choose a token before its preceding tokens, and the token later shapes its neighbors' green lists. Prior work therefore tilts each choice to raise the expected number of green tokens at its own and its neighbors' positions. Building on this objective, we first learn two components that prior work keeps fixed: vocabulary bands that serve as green lists, separate competing candidates and keep the null distribution exact, and a foresight predictor that estimates how each candidate shifts its neighbors' predictions. Second, we count green tokens as the detector does, once per distinct context-token pair, so repetition earns nothing. On WaterBench with LLaDA-8B-Instruct, each learned component raises the z-score at equal distortion, and their gains are nearly additive. With a strong watermark, ours detects at least 96% of responses at a 1% false-positive rate while matching the LLM-judge score of unwatermarked text. Ours also detects more responses on Dream and as many or more on code and question answering without a significant loss in task accuracy.

papers.title: Do Halting Heads Really Save Compute in Looped Language Models?
papers.abstract: Looped language models run each token through the same layers several times, and each run is one iteration. To save compute, an extra layer, the halting head, gives after each iteration the probability that the token stops there, so that easy tokens can stop early. Pretraining models from scratch, up to 1.3B parameters, we find two problems. First, heads trained on a mix of all iterations predict that tokens need under half the iterations, yet under the standard stopping rule tokens run almost every iteration, because this training never scores the single iteration where a token stops. Scoring every iteration instead fixes this, but in our runs it works only with a strong penalty favoring early stops. Second, savings are commonly reported as an average number of iterations per token, but when sequences are generated in batches that run until their slowest token stops, a model without a head is almost as good at that cost. The reported average can therefore overstate the saving. We recommend reporting the iterations tokens actually run, with the stopping threshold and batch size, and give a test, run before training a head, that bounds its gain.

papers.title: Characterizations of the plane and the catenoid as capillary minimal surfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that an annular capillary minimal surface outside the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with one complete embedded end and finite total curvature must be either part of the plane or part of the catenoid. The proofs are based on the use of the Weierstrass data through the Hopf differential and associated holomorphic functions. For a planar end, we control the second fundamental form, while for a catenoidal end, we analyze the Gauss map in more detail using the boundary condition. We also prove nonexistence results for annular free boundary minimal surfaces with one end asymptotic to the end of Enneper's surface, under appropriate conditions. Finally, we establish an exterior analogue of Choe's result on capillary minimal surfaces with vertices.

papers.title: StarRTT: An End-to-End Real-Time Framework for Blind Zone-Free RTT Prediction in Starlink LEO Satellite Networks
papers.abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite mega-constellations such as Starlink require frequent handovers due to high orbital velocities, resulting in substantial Round-Trip Time (RTT) fluctuations. Accurate RTT prediction can mitigate these fluctuations, yet it fundamentally relies on continuously updated serving- satellite information. Existing serving-satellite identification methods typically complete identification only at the end of each scheduling cycle, creating an identification blind zone that limits real-time prediction. To overcome this limitation, we develop StarRTT, an end-to-end real-time framework that eliminates the blind zone by integrating per-second serving-satellite identification with RTT prediction. Within this framework, we propose Real-Time Long Short-Term Memory (RT-LSTM), an LSTM-based RTT prediction model designed to capture both non-stationary RTT evolution and time-varying geometric relationships among the serving satellite, user terminal, and gateways. Specifically, a historical LSTM encodes historical RTT observations and real-time serving-satellite and gateway-relative features, while a future LSTM processes Two-Line Element (TLE)-propagated future features of the identified serving satellite up to the next scheduling instant. Under strict real-time back-testing, RT-LSTM achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.405 ms averaged over all 15 prediction horizons and 15 reference time-slot indices, reducing the error by 4.3 %, 11.6 %, and 22.1 % compared with the existing baseline models, LSTM, StarNet, and Attention-based Spatiotemporal Model (ASTM), respectively. Notably, the reduction over LSTM reaches 12.5 % at the scheduling instant, highlighting the benefit of real-time serving-satellite information when recent RTT observations are limited.

papers.title: The Hardy-Littlewood asymptotic for prime pairs of fixed even difference from a uniform zeta-ratios conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Hardy-Littlewood asymptotic for prime pairs of every fixed positive even difference $h$ from a restricted uniform two-over-two zeta-ratios formula. The formula may have error $O_\varepsilon(U^{\vartheta+\varepsilon})$ for any fixed $1/2\le\vartheta<(39-\sqrt{177})/32$. The real parts of all four shifts lie in $[3/64,5/64]$; their imaginary parts need only have absolute value at most $U^ν$, for a fixed $0<ν\le1/4$. For a fixed real smooth weight supported in $(1,1+1/(25h))$, we obtain an error $O_{h,W,\varepsilon}(x^{-Δ(\vartheta)+\varepsilon})$ in the correlation sum with weight $W(n/x)^2/n$, where $Δ(\vartheta)=7/16-\vartheta+\vartheta/(3-\vartheta)>0$. Adding the Riemann hypothesis improves this error to $O_{h,W,\varepsilon}(x^{\vartheta-7/8+\varepsilon})$. The proof retains the crossed zero residues in Mellin inversion and estimates their mixed term with the logarithmic-derivative integral. Two nonnegative time weights have the same diagonal term and opposite coefficients for the difference $h$. We deduce the logarithmic asymptotic for the weighted prime-pair sum $B_h$ and an asymptotic for the second finite difference of integrals of squared increments of the truncated Chebyshev function. The latter is connected to a logarithmically weighted Möbius approximant in the Nyman-Beurling criterion by finite identities.

papers.title: MG-REPA: Multi-Granularity Representation Alignment for Generative Target Speaker Extraction
papers.abstract: Generative target speaker extraction (TSE) models achieve high-quality extraction, but suffer from considerably slow training convergence. Representation Alignment (REPA) accelerates diffusion transformer training by aligning hidden states with a pre-trained Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) teacher. However, existing alignment in the speech and audio domain operates at a single granularity. For TSE, frame-level alignment leaves the global, time-invariant characteristics of the target speech implicit, whereas utterance-level alignment leaves the time-varying content implicit, even though extracting the target requires both. We propose Multi-Granularity Representation Alignment (MG-REPA), aligning the hidden states with an SSL model at the frame level and a speaker verification model at the utterance level. We further apply temporal normalization to the frame-level target, removing its utterance-level statistics so that each branch concentrates on its granularity. On Libri2Mix, MG-REPA reaches the OVRL and PESQ of a MeanFlow-TSE baseline with $3.0\times$ and $2.1\times$ fewer epochs, respectively. Trained for 750 epochs, it is competitive with the published 2,000-epoch baseline on intrusive metrics while improving non-intrusive metrics. An ablation demonstrates that MG-REPA outperforms alignment at a single granularity.

authors.name: Jung-Woo Choi
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Collection-Date Assignment Redirects Answers in Temporal QA
papers.abstract: A collection date records when a source revision was acquired, not when its contents changed. Can assigning this metadata redirect temporal question answering despite unchanged evidence? Swapping the question day and following day between two revisions lowers later-reference exact match (EM) by 37.6-51.4 percentage points across five open-weight LLMs on 595 Wikipedia pages, replicated on 128 disjoint pages. Previous-day swaps retain 29.0-39.6-point losses on 497 pages. Seven prompt variants, including explicit ignore-collection instructions and archived-revision provenance, retain the effect. Fictional answers and English month-name question dates show that remembered answers and identical date strings are unnecessary. Matched thinking reduces Qwen3.5's penalty from 30.1 to 11.1 points, while native reasoners vary. Two API LLMs show small Wikipedia swap effects and rarely shift to earlier answers on fictional records. Large swap-induced losses concentrate around the question date; swaps between distant dates have much smaller effects. Adding fields containing one observed acquisition date lowers EM relative to omission in three of five LLMs after correction. The diagnostic isolates metadata effects from changing evidence or missing the relevant revision, and provides a practical audit for temporal QA inputs.

papers.title: Anti-coherence Regularized Absolute Scaling for Out-of-Distribution Detection
papers.abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is recognized as a critical problem in AI safety. SCALE is an effective post-hoc OOD detection method in the activation-shaping family that requires no training data and rescales penultimate activations using a percentile-based magnitude ratio. However, this ratio is ill-defined when negative activations are present, since positive and negative contributions cancel within the underlying sum, causing SCALE to degenerate on backbones such as ViT. We address this with an Absolute Fix that computes the ratio over absolute-valued activations rather than discarding negative activations through ReLU. Building on this corrected scale, we propose Anti-coherence regularization, which penalizes the scaling factor by the fraction of a sample's max-logit contributions to the max logit that are sign-mismatched and thereby suppresses unreliable evidence for the predicted class. Despite requiring no access to training data or training labels, our method ties or outperforms activation-shaping methods that rely on training data in terms of AUROC and FPR@95 on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet under the OpenOOD v1.5 protocol.

authors.name: Youngwoong Jin
authors.institution: Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology

authors.name: Hyunsoo Yoon
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Properties and applications of Muckenhoupt $A_1$ growth weights
papers.abstract: For $β\ge0$, let $A_1^{(β)}$ be the class of weights satisfying $$ [w]_{A_1^{(β)}}:= \sup_{0<\varepsilon\le1} \varepsilon^β[w]_{A_{1+\varepsilon}}<\infty. $$ These classes satisfy $A_1\subsetneq A_1^{(β)}\subsetneq\bigcap_{p>1}A_p$ for $β>0$. For every $α\ge0$, we prove that $w\in A_1^{(β)}$ if and only if $$ w\left(\left\{M_{L(\log L)^α}f>λ\right\}\right) \le C\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \frac{|f(x)|}λ \left[ \log\left(e+\frac{|f(x)|}λ\right) \right]^{α+β} w(x)\,\mathrm{d}x. $$ The least constant $C$ is comparable to $[w]_{A_1^{(β)}}$. Also, we obtain corresponding characterizations for Calderón--Zygmund operators and their commutators.

papers.title: CounselPlex: A Stressor-Aware Full-Duplex Counseling Model
papers.abstract: Full-duplex speech models can listen and speak at the same time, enabling natural, low-latency interaction. In counseling, however, these models often focus on the latest utterance and lose track of the seeker's underlying problem. We call this failure Stressor Blindness. We propose CounselPlex, a stressor-aware full-duplex framework that uses two operations. CounselPlex updates a short stressor state during seeker silence and injects this state into <PAD> positions while listening. We also introduce RoPE Position Shift Augmentation (RPSA), which broadens positional coverage during training and improves performance at longer turn depths in our evaluation. LLM-judge evaluations show improved counseling quality and stressor grounding over strong baselines.

authors.name: Yeonju Kim
authors.institution: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety

authors.name: Bella Godiva
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yong Man Ro
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Riesz Transform Bounds Imply Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability of Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that if a $(k+2)$-Ahlfors--David regular measure $μ$ in parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$ has support equal to a parabolic Lipschitz graph with sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(μ)$, then $μ$ is parabolic uniformly rectifiable and the graph is regular parabolic Lipschitz. The result holds for every integer $0\leq k\leq n-1$.

papers.title: DIAL-S2ST: Learning Latency Control for Simultaneous Speech-to-Speech Translation
papers.abstract: We propose DIAL-S2ST, a post-training method for learning inference-time latency control in simultaneous speech-to-speech translation models. Our approach reuses pretrained translation capabilities through self-distillation from lookahead predictions, while limiting the influence of large text distillation losses to account for the imitation gap. This provides supervision for earlier emission without paired target data or reward computation. To make the learned timing adjustable at inference, we jointly train a single LoRA adapter across scales with matched lookahead guidance. Experiments on French-to-English translation with Hibiki demonstrate that only 10 hours of source speech enable this adaptation, providing flexible latency control with a favorable quality-latency trade-off.

authors.name: Jeongsoo Choi
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Joon Son Chung
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Optimization, Optimal Control, and Reinforcement Learning for Robotics
papers.abstract: These lecture notes provide an introduction to optimization, optimal control, and reinforcement learning for robotics, emphasizing their mathematical connections and practical relevance. They present established material compiled and edited by Yonghyeon Lee, rather than new research results. The notes were developed through a human and AI collaborative writing process, with AI assistance in drafting, organizing, and refining the exposition. This first version is a preliminary collection of notes, not yet a fully developed textbook, and currently contains no figures or graphs. The notes may be revised, corrected, and expanded in future versions.

papers.title: Spatiotemporally-resolved differential dynamic microscopy reveals strain-induced deformations in heterogeneous soft materials
papers.abstract: Understanding the microscopic behavior of materials in response to mechanical perturbations is a central challenge in soft matter, yet existing methods, which typically rely on microscopy-based imaging, often struggle with spatial heterogeneity and low signal-to-noise that are characteristic of many soft and biological materials. Additionally, many existing rheo-optical methods focus on the response to macro-scale forces rather than localized perturbations despite the importance of local stresses in biological and industrial applications of soft materials. Here, we present STroboscopically Averaged, time-Resolved Differential Dynamic Microscopy (starDDM) to investigate a sample's deformation across time and distance due to a cyclically applied local force. As proof-of-principle, we use this model-independent and tracer-free approach to map the motions of active cytoskeleton composites imposed by the movement of an optically trapped probe particle embedded within the complex network. We reveal how motor-driven restructuring and varying strain rates tune the magnitude and propagation of the response, which we further show decays with distance from the perturbation. This analytical platform fills a critical gap in micro-rheology, offering a versatile tool for probing the non-equilibrium dynamics of soft materials ranging from biopolymer networks to 3D-printed materials and soft robotics.

papers.title: Hierarchical Absorbing Markov Chain Models for Pooling Sparse Combat Sequence Data
papers.abstract: By viewing tactics in no-gi Brazilian jiu-jitsu (NGJJ) as discrete states, we estimate the transition probabilities of tactical progression, while simultaneously exploring the effects of weight categories on these dynamics with a hierarchical absorbing Markov chain model. We further cluster the weight categories and borrow strength using the Ewens-Pitman attraction of Dahl, Day and Tsai. Random partitions allow us to explore the underlying groupings of these weight categories in terms of their transition patterns. The hierarchical structure enables us to obtain an overall mean estimate of the transition probability matrix along with the individual estimates of the weight categories. Through simulations we find that the proposed model is more flexible than hierarchical methods with no partition or fully-pooled alternatives while sacrificing very little efficiency under model misspecification. Applying this method to NGJJ, we found a back-take is the tactic most likely to lead to achieving submission across all weight categories. In addition, we discovered the lightest (66kg) and heaviest (99kg+) weight categories vary significantly from the others in long-term tactical progression.

papers.title: On Exact Critical-Region Boundaries in Continuous-Time Multiparametric Optimal Control Problems
papers.abstract: Continuous-time multiparametric model predictive control solves the optimal control problem once, offline, for every initial state, and divides the initial-state space into critical regions, each with its own control law and sequence of active constraints. A boundary between two regions is either a hyperplane, given by one linear equation, or curved. The curved boundaries have not been computed to date; a classifier has been trained instead to distinguish the regions, so the partition has been known only approximately. In this paper we show that a curved boundary can be computed exactly, without solving any optimal control problem. The method rests on one property. Once the sequence of active constraints is fixed, together with the instants inside it at which a constraint becomes active or inactive (the switching times) and the instant at which the change of the neighboring region first appears (the event time), every condition on a boundary is a linear equation in the initial state, so the computation of a boundary, curved or not, is exact. We fix one of these instants, a switching time or the event time, and solve the linear equations that correspond to it for the corresponding initial state on the boundary; stepping the fixed instant along the horizon yields the whole boundary. A hyperplane is the case in which no instant is left to fix. We illustrate the method on the Newell-Lee evaporator, which has seven critical regions and eight boundaries, four hyperplanes and four curved, computing one boundary of each type in full with the adjacent regions at its ends.

papers.title: Measuring the Energy Cost of Completing Tasks with Quantized Language-Model Agents
papers.abstract: Quantization reduces the memory and energy needed to serve large language models (LLMs) and AI agents for coding and data analysis can now run on locally hosted LLMs. In practice, this benefit is commonly benchmarked per output token. Yet an agent calls its model repeatedly, runs tools, and revises its work, and quantization can change both how much the agent generates and whether it succeeds. Existing energy studies either compare quantized models on single requests or measure agents at one fixed precision, overlooking how a change in precision plays out across a complete agent task. To address this gap, this paper presents the first characterization of the task-level energy trade-offs of model quantization in locally hosted agents. We develop 29 agent tasks with automatic pass/fail checks in six families, ranging from single-answer SQL analytics to multi-step repository bug fixing, and measure CPU and GPU energy per output token and per completed task for 4-bit and 8-bit versions of two open-weight models on bare-metal NVIDIA A100 nodes with llama$.$cpp. Our findings reveal that 4-bit precision generally saves energy per token, though whether it saves energy per completed task is task dependent and changes with the model and the execution budget (i.e., limits on turns, tokens, and time). We trace this discrepancy to the extra tokens needed to complete a task in full, which translates into using up to 3.5 times as much energy per completed task. These findings offer actionable guidance for developers and operators choosing model precision for agents, showing how tokens per completed task, set against the per-token saving, reveal whether lower precision completes the work with less energy.

papers.title: Polarization-encoded photon statistics for counting dipole emitters
papers.abstract: Counting the emitters within a diffraction-limited region is a prerequisite for localizing overlapping molecules. Under pulsed excitation, each molecule emits at most one photon per pulse, so photon-number-resolved detection can count emitters without resolving them. But the required number of pulses grows steeply with the emitter number. Here we show that polarization, conventionally used to measure the orientations of dipole emitters, also carries information on their number. Because mean polarization-resolved signals are unchanged when every emitter is replaced by multiple dimmer copies, this information resides in the photon statistics within each pulse, which polarization reshapes in two ways. Linearly polarized excitation at three angles increases the sub-Poissonian deficit of the photon count by a factor of 1.5 for any emitter orientation, and detection in four polarization channels reveals the emitter number through how the photons of multiphoton pulses are distributed among the channels. Maximum-likelihood simulations for two to five emitters of unknown orientations and brightnesses show that three-angle excitation reduces the required number of pulses by about 2.3-fold, close to the predicted $1.5^2=2.25$, and that adding four-channel detection raises the reduction to as much as 4.8-fold. These gains require only polarization optics added to photon-number-resolved detection.

papers.title: Coefficient duality and interpolation of Euclidean flag Besov spaces
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to develop the duality theory of the homogeneous Besov spaces associated with the Euclidean flag, using the discrete Littlewood--Paley--Stein analysis. We first establish an exact discrete sampling formula together with bounded analysis and synthesis maps, by which the space is identified with a sequence space of coefficients. The continuous dual is then computed through a coefficient norm. In this computation the geometry of the sampling rectangles plays an essential role: when the spatial exponent is below one, the volume of a dyadic rectangle forces an explicit shift of both smoothness indices. We devote particular attention to the supremum sequence exponent. At that endpoint the closure of the flag test functions is characterized by vanishing scale tails, and the limiting tail is comparable to the distance to this closure; every continuous functional on the full space decomposes into a canonical regular part and a part that annihilates the closure, and the latter may be nonzero. For finite exponents the dual is again a flag Besov space. As applications, finite Calderón sums give a quantitative approximation theorem, and the common analysis and synthesis framework yields real and complex interpolation as well as the lifting property. The arguments are based on the exact sampling formula, scalar maximal estimates and the transpose of one bounded coefficient projection.

authors.name: Chang Li
authors.institution: Suzhou University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The Malt'sev condition for groups is not categorical
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove that the Mal'tsev condition expressing the existence of group operations is not equivalent to a categorical property. More precisely, using pseudo-invertible idempotents, we construct two varieties $\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{V}(f)$ which are equivalent as categories, and such that $\mathcal{V}$ admits group operations, whereas $\mathcal{V}(f)$ does not. We also show that those Mal'tsev conditions which are equivalent to a categorical property have a trivial spectrum.

papers.title: Binary Quadratic Forms, Shintani Lifts, and Twisted L-Values
papers.abstract: Let $F\in S_{2k}^{new}(M,χ^2)$ be a Hecke newform, and $D$ a fundamental discriminant with $(-1)χ(-1)D>0$. Via the Shimura Correspondence, we get associated modular forms of half-integral weight, and Waldspurger showed that for such $g=\sum c_nq^n \in S_{k+1/2}(4M',χ;F)$, if $c_{|D|}(g)\neq 0$, then $|c_{|D|}(g)|^2 \propto |D|^{k-1/2}L(F\otimes \overlineχ\otimes χ_D,k)$. Kohnen refined this in the case that $f\in S_{2k}^{new}(N)$ for $N$ odd and squarefree, making explicit $|c_{|D|}(g)|^2$ for $g \in S^+_{k+1/2}(4N;f)$. However, $c_{|D|}(g)=0$ unless $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)=w_p(f)$ for all $p|N$. In this paper, we produce more generally $g \in S^+_{k+1/2}(4\ \mathrm{lcm}(N,N_1^2),χ;f\otimes χ)$, where $χ$ is a character of odd squarefree conductor $N_1$, using a family of generalised Shimura/Shintani maps $Ψ_χ^D,{Ψ_χ^D}^*$ due to Kojima and Tokuno. Extending their work (and Kohnen's), we compute its Petersson norm, and give an explicit formula for all the $|c_m(g)|^2$. The key technical ingredient is an explicit set of representatives for $L^0_{M_1,M}(M_1^2D^2)/Γ_0(M)$ of binary quadratic forms. We also use a new multiplicity-one result based on work of Kohnen, Ueda, and Waldspurger. In the case $N_1|N$, we reconstruct forms previously considered by Baruch-Mao and Prasanna, which change Kohnen's condition to $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)=-w_p(f)$ for all $p|N_1$, thus relating twisted $L$-values to squares of Fourier coefficients for all classes of discriminants.

authors.name: Mark Chambers
authors.institution: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center

papers.title: Pairing Matters: Performance, Failures, and Efficiency in Lightweight Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Self-hosting coding agents is often necessary for software-engineering teams that must keep proprietary code and development traces within controlled infrastructure. Lightweight, open-weight models make such deployment more feasible by reducing hardware requirements, while strong results on repository-level benchmarks demonstrate their potential for demanding coding tasks. Deploying these models as coding agents requires pairing them with an agent harness, making their joint performance a key deployment consideration. Yet existing leaderboards primarily report fixed harness-model configurations rather than controlled comparisons across alternative pairings. To address this gap, we investigate harness-model interactions through a controlled full-factorial evaluation of six open-source harnesses and three lightweight coding models across 100 SWE-bench Verified tasks, producing 1,800 graded runs under common serving, metering, and grading conditions. For the same model, resolution rates differ by up to 44 percentage points across harnesses, while harness rankings change across models. We apply an evidence-based failure taxonomy to 1,100 unsuccessful runs and find substantial differences in failure patterns across harness-model pairings. A model's dominant failure modes under one harness need not dominate under another. Efficiency is similarly dependent on the pairing: even among model-directed loop harnesses, charged tokens per resolved task vary by more than 20-fold. These findings make harness-model selection a central deployment decision for lightweight coding agents. Strong performance with one harness or model does not guarantee similar results with another. We translate these findings into practitioner guidance for pairing selection, token-efficiency assessment, and trajectory-informed harness engineering, and release the complete experimental records and analysis artifacts.

papers.title: Banded Chaos and Time-Semicrystalline Order
papers.abstract: Recent work has introduced the notion of a time semicrystal, a driven nonequilibrium regime in which subharmonic temporal order survives inside deterministic chaos. Here we revisit this phenomenology from the viewpoint of classical nonlinear dynamics. Banded chaotic attractors consist of a finite number of chaotic sectors cyclically permuted by stroboscopic evolution, allowing discrete subharmonic spectral components to coexist with a broadband chaotic continuum. Exemplified through the driven Duffing oscillator and the logistic map, this structure naturally reproduces the characteristic signatures of time-semicrystalline dynamics. Within this framework, periodic subharmonic motion can enter chaos through the familiar period-doubling cascade while retaining a well-defined temporal skeleton governed by the universal Feigenbaum scaling. Temporal order within chaos can also reorganize or collapse through distinct mechanisms, producing continuous or abrupt transitions that may be intertwined with symmetry changes. These results connect time-semicrystal phenomenology with established structures of dissipative nonlinear dynamics, showing that its essential ingredients already arise in standard nonlinear systems and providing a simple framework for extending and testing the paradigm in more complex, many-body, and experimental settings.

papers.title: On quasi-Albanese morphisms for log canonical Calabi-Yau pairs II
papers.abstract: Centering on quasi-Albanese morphisms, we prove several structural theorems for Calabi-Yau pairs.

authors.name: Yiming Zhu
authors.institution: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology

papers.title: Semantically Rich, Metrically Affect-Blind: A Geometric Blind Spot in Modern Text Embedders
papers.abstract: We report a systematic dissociation in modern text embedders: sentiment is almost perfectly decodable from their embeddings, yet almost entirely absent from their metric. Across eleven frozen encoders spanning 2021 to 2026, including 2026-generation models and the 4B-parameter LLM embedder Qwen3-Embedding-4B, a linear probe recovers sentence polarity at up to 91.3% accuracy while cosine similarity separates polarity by a margin of only 0.003-0.064. Qwen3-Embedding-4B, the strongest probe in the panel, reaches 91.3% probe accuracy but only 64.3 retrieval MAP. Because retrieval, clustering, deduplication, and retrieval-augmented generation operate on the metric rather than on a trained probe, these systems are effectively blind to information their encoder demonstrably contains. A task-conditioning control suggests this reflects the pretraining objective rather than a prompting artifact: conditioning Jina-v5 on its classification task rather than its retrieval task recovers only about half of the MAP gain that injection achieves on the same weights (63.2 to 73.8, versus 85.1), and leaves the alignment gap essentially unchanged. Sentiment-Injected Sentence Embeddings (SISE) train a small (0.13M-0.69M-parameter) supervised-contrastive head on a frozen encoder in seconds on a CPU, using the labelled training set. The head improves every encoder released since 2022 on full-data probe accuracy (up to +5.8 points), retrieval MAP (up to +26.0) and polarity margin (7-61x). This is a specialization, not a free gain: the compact 128-d head loses 38-41 Spearman points on STS-B, while a fused variant that concatenates it with the base embedding loses 2.4-12.0. With the head, a 0.6B encoder at 128 dimensions matches a 4B encoder given the same head (91.8 vs. 90.3 MAP). We release a CPU-reproducible pipeline and a reusable diagnostic, the Attribute Alignment Gap.

papers.title: Optimal Graphon Control of Collective Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study optimal control of non-linear graphon dynamics in which the interaction kernel itself is the control. Motivated by opinion formation in social networks, we ask how changing who influences whom can steer a population toward a desired outcome. We develop a framework using interaction kernels with bounded variation in the receiver label, providing compactness while accommodating finite networks. We prove existence of an optimal pair and show that finite-agent approximations recover the continuum optimal value under successive refinement of the network and initial data, with subsequential convergence of suitably chosen discrete optimizers. Numerical experiments use neural networks to approximate optimal controls for bounded-confidence and graphon Kuramoto dynamics, illustrating how changes in interactions can prevent fragmentation and promote synchronization.

papers.title: Gaze Under Strain: How Oculomotor Behavior Tracks Cybersickness Progression in VR
papers.abstract: Cybersickness remains a major barrier to comfortable, accessible virtual reality (VR). Arising from mismatches between visual and vestibular signals, it places sustained demands on gaze stabilization and visual processing. Because gaze is the mechanism through which users actively sample the virtual environment, cybersickness-induced disruptions may alter both what users perceive and how discomfort itself emerges. Yet, how eye-movement behavior evolves alongside discomfort during prolonged VR exposure remains poorly understood. We present a behavioral analysis of eye-tracking data from 19 participants navigating a realistic virtual environment over a 20-minute session, with discomfort rated repeatedly throughout the experiment. Linear mixed-effects models examined gaze constructs spanning fixation stability, visual exploration, and gaze allocation as functions of discomfort, exposure duration, and their interaction. Our results show that fixation stability degraded progressively with increasing discomfort, with the effect strengthening over time. Visual exploration showed no marginal discomfort effect but exhibited significant discomfort-by-time interactions, indicating that saccadic behavior adapts dynamically rather than responding uniformly to discomfort. Gaze allocation was not associated with discomfort but shifted systematically with time. These findings show that cybersickness does not uniformly disrupt gaze. Instead, different aspects of eye-movement behavior respond differently and change in ways that only become visible when discomfort is tracked repeatedly over time. Understanding how gaze evolves during cybersickness progression provides the behavioral grounding needed to better interpret how discomfort shapes the user's visual experience of immersive environments and to design more sensitive detection approaches.

papers.title: Duality of Shortfall Aversion
papers.abstract: Shortfall aversion describes a form of consumption habit formation in which an individual's utility depends on consumption relative to the historical consumption peak. This study develops a duality framework for a broad class of utility functions, with and without discounting, avoiding the need for determining the local optimality required by the HJB approaches commonly adopted in the literature. We show that shortfall aversion can instead be incorporated directly into the dual problem through a singular-control mechanism characterized by a variational inequality. Furthermore, we establish that the resulting value function strictly dominates those obtained in the existing literature while remaining attainable under an admissible optimal control. We demonstrate that the suboptimality of existing solutions stems from their myopic treatment of updates to the consumption peak, whereas our duality approach enlarges the admissible class to treat the consumption peak as a separate nondecreasing control and determines its optimal evolution through duality, accounting for future consumption opportunities. These results reveal a previously unrecognized advantage of the dual formulation and provide a more general and flexible framework for consumption optimization under shortfall aversion.

papers.title: Shorter Is Not Cheaper: A Controlled Comparison of Declarative Animation Specifications and Free-Form Code for LLM-Generated Explanations
papers.abstract: Chat assistants increasingly answer conceptual questions with interactive, animated explanations, generated either as free-form HTML/JavaScript or as declarative specifications that a fixed runtime plays. The declarative route is widely expected to be cheaper, faster and more reliable, because its outputs are shorter and constrained. We test this expectation in controlled comparisons whose hypotheses and analysis plans were frozen before the runs. We designed ExplainSpec, a time-indexed declarative animation format, and an observation contract that makes every generated explanation programmatically inspectable; validated, pacing-agnostic checkers score 20 explanation requests from five domains. Three Claude models (360 jobs) and, in a follow-up, the open-weight Qwen3-14B with thinking enabled and disabled (240 jobs) answered every request in both formats. For every model the specifications were 25-48% shorter in answer tokens (output excluding reasoning), yet with reasoning enabled total output fell significantly only for the largest Claude model and no model generated significantly faster. The reasons differed. The Claude models reasoned far more before writing specifications (exploratory; for the two larger models, from 15-20% to 85-88% of generations). Qwen3-14B reasoned about as much in both formats (a pre-registered test of this shift was not supported), and its shorter answers saved little against a reasoning trace more than twice as long. Nor were specifications more reliable: free-form pages were valid after one repair round in 95-100% of jobs for every model, whereas Qwen3-14B produced valid specifications in only 33% of jobs and passed all semantic tests in 17% (HTML/JavaScript: 62%). For reasoning models, a shorter format alone therefore does not make generation cheaper, faster or more reliable, and a format learned in context can cost reliability.

papers.title: Modified scattering for the 3D Hartree equation with singular external potentials
papers.abstract: We establish modified scattering for the three-dimensional Hartree equation with Coulomb interaction and singular external potentials, including repulsive Coulomb and inverse-square potentials. In the defocusing case, the result holds for arbitrary initial data in $H^{0,1}(\mathbb R^3)\cap H^{1,0}(\mathbb R^3)$. In particular, we obtain large-data modified scattering for the flat defocusing Hartree equation. For the focusing problem with repulsive Coulomb potential $V(x)=κ|x|^{-1}$, we prove radial modified scattering under the sharp mass condition $|λ|\|u_0\|_2^2\leq 2κ$, including the endpoint, and construct standing waves at every larger mass. Our argument obtains strong $L^2$ convergence from rescaled energy and comparison with a frozen-field evolution.

papers.title: Total eight-colorings of maximal planar graphs of maximum degree six
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite simple maximal planar graph of maximum degree at most six admits a total eight-coloring. We first show that every proper vertex four-coloring of a subcubic graph extends to a total five-coloring. A curvature inequality for boundary walks then gives a matching decomposition of four-connected triangulations with degrees five and six, extending their prescribed vertex four-colorings to total eight-colorings. In a minimum counterexample, two local boundary colorings force the degree-four vertices to have disjoint neighborhoods. A characterization of the local extension obstructions permits these vertices to be restored simultaneously. The proof uses Hamiltonian-connectedness of four-connected planar graphs and Kardoš's Hamiltonicity theorem for three-connected cubic planar graphs.

papers.title: $G_0$ of complete split toric varieties
papers.abstract: We compute the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves for complete split toric surfaces having a smooth 2-dimensional cone in its fan. We show that it is free abelian, of rank equal to the number of rays in the fan. We give a partial generalization of this to all complete split toric varieties.

authors.name: Zeyu Shen
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Weighted and nonlocal Poisson equations on domains with capacity density conditions
papers.abstract: We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for global Hölder solvability of weighted Poisson equations and related fractional problems. On domains satisfying a capacity density condition, a nonnegative measure with bounded support depth admits a bounded globally Hölder continuous zero-boundary solution if and only if it satisfies an interior Morrey-type growth condition. Conversely, uniform boundary decay estimates for solutions with localized nonnegative sources characterize the capacity density condition. Analogous characterizations are established for the restricted and spectral fractional Laplacians. Our approach is based on weighted strong barriers and also yields two-weight Hardy inequalities, compact trace embeddings, and global Hölder solvability for nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators.

papers.title: Meromorphic approximation of holomorphic maps into algebraically elliptic projective varieties
papers.abstract: We show that holomorphic maps from a neighborhood of a compact set in a Stein space to an algebraically elliptic smooth projective variety can be approximated by meromorphic maps, provided that the map extends continuously to the whole space and the compact set is convex with respect to a submonoid of the Picard group. The proof uses algebraic sprays and their polynomial lifts to affine cones, which we call conic lifts. Rational sprays, which generalize algebraic sprays, extend the result to maps avoiding the exceptional set of a rational spray. We also show that, for smooth projective varieties, the existence of an algebraic spray which is dominating at some point is a birational invariant.

papers.title: Sensitivity-Guided Parameter Estimation of Bubbly Liquid via a Nonlinear Wave Equation and Physics-InformedNeuralNetworks
papers.abstract: Interactions between ultrasound and microbubbles underlie a range of biomedical and industrial applications, yet predicting how the physical parameters of the medium and bubbles govern nonlinear wave propagation remains difficult. This study proposes a parameter estimation framework that combines a Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers (KdVB) equation, describing weakly nonlinear wave propagation in a bubbly liquid, with a physics-informed neural network (PINN). The contributions are threefold. First, the PINN reproduces the reference solution of the governing equation in the forward problem, with a near-zero prediction error at the initial time that confirms the initial condition is enforced exactly as intended. Second, prior to inverse estimation, a sensitivity analysis is introduced that quantifies, at both the coefficient and solution levels, how each of eight physical parameters influences the KdVB equation, allowing the expected difficulty of estimating each parameter to be assessed in advance. Third, based on this assessment, single-parameter inverse estimation is performed for seven of the eight parameters using the PINN. Liquid viscosity, bubble initial radius, liquid density, sound speed, and liquid pressure are estimated with errors of 0.8-2.1%, the polytropic exponent converges only partially, and the surface tension coefficient cannot be estimated at all, consistent with the sensitivity analysis. These results establish a general framework for identifying and estimating the physical parameters governing nonlinear wave propagation in bubbly liquids from observed waveform data.

authors.name: Shota Deguchi
authors.institution: Fukui City Museum of Natural History

papers.title: Information Requirements for Resolving Implementation Impossibilities
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for assessing implementation impossibilities through the information required to resolve them. Domain covers describe information used to select a mechanism without restricting admissible preferences. Coarsening a cover weakens the required information. In quasi-linear public decision problems with a status quo, we study two impossibilities of dominant-strategy implementation: combining efficiency and individual rationality with either budget feasibility or budget balancedness. Under an interval cover based on bounds on maximal social surplus, we characterize the social choice rules implementable in dominant strategies and satisfying the first set of axioms. Under a surplus-level cover based on exact surplus levels, we obtain the corresponding characterization for the second set of axioms. Both covers are minimal: no strictly coarser cover permits implementation under the respective requirements. These economically interpretable minimal covers deepen our understanding of the informational severity of each impossibility.

papers.title: Rough path lifts of multifractional Brownian motions
papers.abstract: We show that multifractional Brownian motions (mBms) can be lifted to geometric rough paths. One of the main ingredients in the proof is a decomposition of mBms via the Lemarié-Meyer orthogonal wavelet basis, which is introduced in the context of multiresolution analysis. As a consequence, we are able to construct solutions to rough differential equations driven by mBms.

Here we focus on how to construct rough paths associated with Gaussian processes including fBm. Some sufficient conditions for constructing rough paths associated with Gaussian processes are known. If Gaussian processes satisfy one of the sufficient conditions, we can construct geometric rough paths associated with the processes. The first condition is known as the Coutin-Qian condition ([7]). The authors constructed geometric rough paths associated with fBms by establishing the sufficient condition. We precisely state this condition in Definition 2.6 and use it to show our main results. papers.title: Perfectly aperiodic asymmetric scalable metasurface based on the hat monotile
papers.abstract: Metasurfaces are conventionally designed on periodic lattices, which renders their electromagnetic response spatially uniform and leaves the spatial arrangement itself unused as an information-bearing design resource. In this study, we propose and numerically validate a metasurface built on an aperiodic monotile: the recently discovered "hat" polykite, a single tile mathematically guaranteed to tile the plane only nonperiodically. The twelve distinguishable orientations of the hat serve as a natural design basis; each carries resonant elements tuned to one of twelve absorption frequencies between 4.600 and 4.914 GHz, transcribing the provable aperiodicity and mirror asymmetry of the geometry into the electromagnetic response. Gaussian-beam scanning over a compositionally unique 6 times 6 grid yields irregular, position-dependent electromagnetic signatures whose pairwise separations reach beyond 6 dB. In particular, coherence-guided selection of multiple frequencies increases the stable rank of the position-signature matrix from 1.0 to approximately 1.6 with three frequency components, whereas the accumulation of mutually similar electromagnetic features fails to add effective dimensions, demonstrating that properly selected multifrequency characteristics enhance the spatial distinguishability embedded in the surface. A shift-correlation analysis in which the cosine similarity never exceeds 0.5 confirms that the response inherits the absence of translational order from the tiling. Compatible with standard printed-circuit fabrication, the aperiodic metasurface design establishes a deterministic route toward position-identifiable electromagnetic environments for localization, chipless identification, and integrated sensing and communication.

papers.title: Head Dimension Matters in Language Models for Long-Context Retrieval
papers.abstract: Multi-head attention retrieves and combines context representations through query--key interactions and value aggregation, with head dimension constraining the per-head representation space. In long-context processing, it remains unclear whether allocating a fixed parameter budget to fewer, wider heads improves information retrieval. In this paper, we investigate how head dimension affects the performance of long-context retrieval tasks. Our empirical studies reveal that pretraining loss and short-context non-retrieval task performance are not affected much by head dimension, while long-context retrieval performance improves with wider heads at fixed model sizes. We find that models with wider heads have a higher proportion of retrieval heads, associating more parameters with retrieval. Our ablation studies also show that the retrieval performance improves with wider heads even when the projection weights in attention modules are frozen during long-context continual pretraining, suggesting that wider heads not only benefit updates in attention modules but lead to more effective adaptation of components such as embeddings and MLPs.

papers.title: Existence and Absence of Spin-Glass Phases on Migdal--Kadanoff Hierarchical Lattices: A Complete Classification
papers.abstract: We consider the Ising spin-glass model on Migdal--Kadanoff (MK) hierarchical lattices, characterized by the fractal dimension $d=1+\log s/\log b$, where $s$ and $b$ denote the number of parallel branches and the number of bonds in series within each branch, respectively. For independent Gaussian couplings, we rigorously establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for arbitrary integers $b,s\ge2$. We prove that a finite-temperature spin-glass phase exists whenever \[ \frac{b}{\sqrt{s}} \left( \frac{b\sqrt{s(s-1)}}{bs-1} \right)^{s-1}<1. \] In particular, this condition holds for all three-dimensional MK hierarchical lattices ($d=3$, or equivalently $s=b^2$), regardless of the choice of $b$. Conversely, we prove the absence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for fractal dimensions $d<1+\log17/\log6\approx2.58$, as well as in the large-$b$ limit for any fixed $d<3$. In the intermediate regime $1+\log17/\log6\le d<3$, we provide a finite-step procedure to determine the presence or absence of spin-glass order, which depends on $b$ and $s$. Our results provide a complete characterization of finite-temperature spin-glass order on MK hierarchical lattices.

papers.title: The Impact of Inclination, Redshift, and Mass Ratio Selection on Cosmological Constraints from Bright Sirens Beyond Conventional Fisher Approximations
papers.abstract: Future generations of gravitational-wave observatories are projected to detect up to thousands bright siren events within a decade of operation. However, the precision of these cosmological forecasts depends heavily on the astrophysical assumptions embedded within the simulation pipelines. In this work, we systematically investigate the impact of variations in the binary mass ratio ($q$), the maximum observable inclination angle ($ι_{\max}$), and the maximum redshift ($z_{\max}$) on the constraints of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) and the matter density parameter ($Ω_m$). We perform our analyses based on the GWDALI framework, the GW Doublet Approximation, and the phenomenological waveform approximant IMRPhenomD. By adopting sets of non-spinning binary neutron star populations we explore the impact of astrophysical parameters on the constraints of cosmological parameters. Our results reveal a clear dichotomy in the observational requirements: while the statistical uncertainty on $H_0$ falls below the falls below approximately $1.3\%$ level for $N \ge 400$ events and drops under $0.9\%$ once $N \ge 800$, a deep-redshift catalog ($z_{\max} \ge 1.0$) is strictly required to effectively break parameter degeneracies and constrain the global geometry through $Ω_m$. Furthermore, expanding the maximum inclination cutoff from the conservative $20^{\circ}$ up to $40^{\circ}$ substantially mitigates the correlation between distance and inclination.

authors.institution: Universidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro

papers.title: Graph distance and percolation dimension of three-dimensional Brownian motion
papers.abstract: We prove that the minimum Hausdorff dimension of a continuous curve joining $W_0$ to $W_1$ within the range $W([0,1])$ of a three-dimensional Brownian motion is almost surely a deterministic constant $γ_3\in(1,5/3]$. Moreover, we construct continuum many simple curves with pairwise distinct images that attain this minimum. Each curve has box dimension $γ_3$ and admits a parametrization that is $β$-Hölder for every $0<β<1/γ_3$. To identify $γ_3$, we partition Brownian time into $n$ equal intervals and form a graph by joining pairs with intersecting ranges. We show that its endpoint graph distance and diameter have a common deterministic almost sure growth exponent $θ$ and that $γ_3=2θ$. We also establish $n^{pθ+o(1)}$ growth for their $p$-th moments, for every $p>0$.

papers.title: Measurement speed limit and Cramér-Rao bound for time-averaged estimators
papers.abstract: We consider a measured system $X$ containing a parameter $θ$ of interest and the problem of estimating this parameter by observing a second, coupled measurement system $Y$. We show that, in thermodynamic equilibrium, the Fisher information of $Y$ associated with the parameter is bounded by that of $X$, implying that conservative interactions between $X$ and $Y$ reduce the precision of parameter estimation. Conversely, out of equilibrium, we show that the Fisher information of $Y$ can exceed that of $X$, so that non-conservative interactions can potentially increase the precision of parameter estimation. For idealized, back-action-free measurements, where the coupling to $Y$ does not perturb $X$, we derive a speed limit for the increase of Fisher information of $Y$. This speed limit only depends on the properties of the measured system $X$ and places a fundamental bound on the precision of any back-action-free measurement. As a corollary, we obtain a generalized Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for time-averaged estimators. We illustrate our results for linear dynamics and suggest a scheme for disturbance-free non-equilibrium sensing with improved accuracy.

papers.title: The elastic figure-eight knot is not planar
papers.abstract: We prove that every elastic knot in any non-torus twist knot class is not planar. In particular, this disproves a numerically motivated planarity conjecture for elastic figure-eight knots.

papers.title: Introducing the GION Lightcone Simulation Suite for Multi-Wavelength Large-Scale Structure Cosmology
papers.abstract: We present the GION (Ginkaku Lightcone Multi-wavelength Simulation Project) simulation suite: 10 full-sky high-resolution cosmological lightcone simulations and their associated products for multi-wavelength large-scale structure cosmology. We use the TreePM $N$-body code GINKAKU, which is highly optimized in the massively parallel environment, and integrate the on-the-fly lightcone construction technique. Each lightcone simulation is run with $6144^3$ particles in a volume of $(1.5 \, h^{-1} \, \mathrm{Gpc})^3$, which corresponds to a particle mass of $1.28 \times 10^9 \, h^{-1} \, \mathrm{M}_\odot$, and extends to $z = 5$. The fine mass resolution and the depth of the lightcone simulations allow us to resolve dark matter halos down to $10^{11} \, h^{-1} \, \mathrm{M}_\odot$ in the high-redshift Universe, which is crucial for applications to the Stage-IV cosmological surveys. The fundamental statistics of the simulations, including the matter power spectrum, halo power spectrum, and halo mass function, are validated against theoretical predictions. We also generate various large-scale structure observables from the lightcone outputs: the dark matter halo catalogs, mock galaxy samples, weak lensing convergence maps, and thermal and kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ and kSZ) maps. The angular power spectra of these observables, including the cross-correlation between weak lensing and the tSZ effect, are in good agreement with theoretical predictions, demonstrating that the suite provides mutually consistent multi-wavelength observables on the same lightcone. The GION simulation suite will be publicly available and can be used for various cosmological analyses to address the observational systematic effects and validate theoretical models.
